    <itunes:summary><![CDATA[Cloud Security Podcast by Google focuses on security in the cloud, delivering security from the cloud, and all things at the intersection of security and cloud. Of course, we will also cover what we are doing in Google Cloud to help keep our users' data safe and workloads secure. 

We're going to do our best to avoid security theater, and cut to the heart of real security questions and issues. Expect us to question threat models and ask if something is done for the data subject's benefit or just for organizational benefit. 

We hope you'll join us if you're interested in where technology overlaps with process and bumps up against organizational design. We're hoping to attract listeners who are happy to hear conventional wisdom questioned, and who are curious about what lessons we can and can't keep as the world moves from on-premises computing to cloud computing.]]></itunes:summary>

    <description><![CDATA[Cloud Security Podcast by Google focuses on security in the cloud, delivering security from the cloud, and all things at the intersection of security and cloud. Of course, we will also cover what we are doing in Google Cloud to help keep our users' data safe and workloads secure. 

We're going to do our best to avoid security theater, and cut to the heart of real security questions and issues. Expect us to question threat models and ask if something is done for the data subject's benefit or just for organizational benefit. 

We hope you'll join us if you're interested in where technology overlaps with process and bumps up against organizational design. We're hoping to attract listeners who are happy to hear conventional wisdom questioned, and who are curious about what lessons we can and can't keep as the world moves from on-premises computing to cloud computing.]]></description>

      <title>EP292 Inside Chrome Security: AI Patching, Agents, Rust, and … Your Tabs</title>
      <itunes:title>EP292 Inside Chrome Security: AI Patching, Agents, Rust, and … Your Tabs</itunes:title>
      <pubDate>Tue, 25 Aug 2026 14:01:00 +0000</pubDate>
      <guid isPermaLink="false"><![CDATA[83fbee60-6c4a-4769-991c-d430aa276e64]]></guid>
      <link><![CDATA[https://cloudsecuritypodcast.libsyn.com/ep292-inside-chrome-security-ai-patching-agents-rust-and-your-tabs]]></link>
      <description><![CDATA[<p dir="ltr">Guests:</p> <ul> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation">Jasika Bawa, Group Product Manager, Chrome Security</li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation">Doug Turner, Engineering Director, Chrome Security</li> </ul> <p dir="ltr">Topics:</p> <ul> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation">Gemini agent harness found a sandbox escape that survived in the codebase for 13 years! How did that happen and how did that bug get noticed among what's surely a tidal wave of bugs being found by the machines?</li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation">Chrome 149 and 150 fixed over a thousand security bugs—surpassing the last 23 milestones combined. That is a massive spike! T<a href= "https://blog.google/security/chrome-stronger-with-every-update/">he blog</a> explains it's possible by having 'fixing agents' and 'critic agents' working in a loop that mimics human code reviews. I have to ask: how much of this is real, high-quality engineering, and how much of it is just two robots agreeing to grade each other on a curve?</li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation">Historically, pushing updates was a monumental, scheduled event. Now, you're piloting two security releases a week to combat fast-moving attacks. That sounds like a direct route to developer burnout, and a complete nightmare for enterprise IT admins who just want their systems to stay stable. How are we balancing the need to protect users from N-day exploits versus making everyone play security whack-a-mole?</li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation">I want to learn more about this long-term vision so let's address the elephant in the browser: nobody wants to restart Chrome. Personally, I have about 50 tabs open right now, and restarting feels like risking throwing my short-term memory into a woodchipper. You're talking about 'dynamic patching' that replaces background child processes on the fly without a restart, and you've rolled out a 'zero window auto-restart' on macOS. First off, are my tabs safe? Second, is dynamic patching actually going to work seamlessly, or is it just going to crash my Renderer mid-session and blame it on the GPU? If this is real, it's really amazing. </li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation">Tell us about the "spannification" effort and the migration to Rust. There's two parallel technical safety efforts going on to–as we like to say at Google–eliminate classes of vulnerabilities. Tell us about the engineering efforts behind the C++ spans and the Rust journey! </li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation">Ok I'd be a terrible Allan Friedman disciple if I didn't ask the supply chain question. First, Chrome has over 2,300 third-party dependencies. That's wild. How are we handling that?</li> </ul> <p dir="ltr">Resources:</p> <ul> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation"><a href= "https://youtu.be/pCXT8lQqg_U">Video version</a></li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation"><a href= "https://blog.google/security/chrome-stronger-with-every-update/">"Stronger with every update: How we're making Chrome and the web safer in the AI Era"</a> blog</li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation"><a href= "https://cloud.withgoogle.com/cloudsecurity/podcast/next-special-improving-browser-security-in-the-new-era-of-work/"> EP88 Improving Browser Security in the New Era of Work</a></li> </ul>]]></description>
      
      <content:encoded><![CDATA[<p dir="ltr">Guests:</p> <ul> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation">Jasika Bawa, Group Product Manager, Chrome Security</li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation">Doug Turner, Engineering Director, Chrome Security</li> </ul> <p dir="ltr">Topics:</p> <ul> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation">Gemini agent harness found a sandbox escape that survived in the codebase for 13 years! That is a massive spike! Now, you're piloting two security releases a week to combat fast-moving attacks. That sounds like a direct route to developer burnout, and a complete nightmare for enterprise IT admins who just want their systems to stay stable. How are we balancing the need to protect users from N-day exploits versus making everyone play security whack-a-mole?</li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation">I want to learn more about this long-term vision so let's address the elephant in the browser: nobody wants to restart Chrome. Personally, I have about 50 tabs open right now, and restarting feels like risking throwing my short-term memory into a woodchipper.       <title>EP291  Ruthless Prioritization: How CISOs Can Execute a Minimum Viable Security Program</title>
      <itunes:title>EP291  Ruthless Prioritization: How CISOs Can Execute a Minimum Viable Security Program</itunes:title>
      <pubDate>Tue, 18 Aug 2026 00:47:00 +0000</pubDate>
      <guid isPermaLink="false"><![CDATA[34756105-ebcf-4cd4-8fa7-6d06572e12a8]]></guid>

      <description><![CDATA[<p dir="ltr">Guest:</p> <ul> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation"><a href= "https://www.linkedin.com/in/mike-armistead-1164715/">Mike Armistead</a>,  CEO, Pulse Security AI</li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation"><a href= "https://www.linkedin.com/in/danlamorena/">Dan Lamorena</a>, Chief Go-To-Market Officer,  <a href= "https://pulsesecurity.ai/">Pulse Security AI</a></li> </ul> <p dir="ltr">Topics: </p> <ul> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation">You've described Pulse as an 'operational management platform for cybersecurity leaders.' What does a security management platform look like in practice? </li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation">How does Pulse bridge this 'translation layer' gap? How do you help a CISO transition from presenting patch rates and MTTD to discussing liability exposure and business capital allocation?</li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation">What actually gets better when someone works with Pulse? Other than, of course, your ARR numbers for your next funding round?</li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation">What is the single most surprising or alarming disconnect you've identified in your CISO and Board Engagement Survey? </li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation">You've introduced the concept of the 'Minimum Viable Security Program (MV(S)P)' and emphasized that 'focus is power.' In an era of non-stop vendor noise, compliance updates, and emerging AI threats, how does Pulse help a CISO ruthlessly prioritize and execute their MV(S)P without getting distracted by the noise?</li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation">Your company is officially 'Pulse Security AI,' so AI is central to your brand.     <item>
      <title>EP289 Software Engineering vs. Software Craft: How Google Scalably Eliminates Classes of Vulnerabilities</title>
      <itunes:title>EP289 Software Engineering vs. Software Craft: How Google Scalably Eliminates Classes of Vulnerabilities</itunes:title>
      <pubDate>Mon, 03 Aug 2026 12:00:00 +0000</pubDate>
      <guid isPermaLink="false"><![CDATA[0fcf1d4e-d676-4ce0-b987-fb1b4a04a31f]]></guid>
      <link><![CDATA[https://cloudsecuritypodcast.libsyn.com/ep289-software-engineering-vs-software-craft-how-google-scalably-eliminates-classes-of-vulnerabilities]]></link>
      <description><![CDATA[<p><span data-markdown-start-index="141">How do you build the foundations for a secure Google-scale enterprise that stays secure</span> <em><span data-markdown-start-index="196">even if</span></em> <span data-markdown-start-index="204">an AI is writing the code and nobody has time to review it? In this episode, hosts Timothy Peacock and Anton Chuvakin sit down with Christoph Kern, Principal Security Engineer at Google, to look under the hood of "secure-by-design." They trace Google's 15-year engineering journey to fundamentally eliminate entire classes of vulnerabilities rather than just playing whack-a-mole with bugs after they are written.</span></p> <p><strong><span data-markdown-start-index="617">🛠️ Software Engineering vs. Software Craft:</span></strong><span data-markdown-start-index= "667"> Why Google ditched "be careful" programming checklists in favor of hard compiler and framework-level invariants that make security defects physically impossible to build.</span></p> <p><strong><span data-markdown-start-index="837">📦 Hiding the       <title>EP279 Native Cloud Security: Is 'Good Enough' Actually Winning?</title>
      <itunes:title>EP279 Native Cloud Security: Is &#39;Good Enough&#39; Actually Winning?</itunes:title>
      <pubDate>Mon, 25 May 2026 14:11:00 +0000</pubDate>
      <guid isPermaLink="false"><![CDATA[80a55bf9-dc26-4b2f-bfd3-a402e779e590]]></guid>
      <link><![CDATA[https://cloudsecuritypodcast.libsyn.com/ep279-native-cloud-security-is-good-enough-actually-winning]]></link>
      <description><![CDATA[<p dir="ltr">Guests:</p> <ul> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation"><a href= "https://www.linkedin.com/in/galordo/">Gal Ordo</a>, Co-founder & CPO @ <a href="https://native.security/">Native</a></li> </ul> <p><strong> </strong>Topics:<strong> </strong></p> <ul> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation"><a href= "https://cloud.withgoogle.com/cloudsecurity/podcast/ep186-cloud-security-tools-trust-the-cloud-provider-or-go-third-party-an-epic-debate-anton-vs-tim/"> In Episode 186</a>, we debated 'Native vs. Third-Party' as a binary choice. Native seems to be a third-party vendor whose entire existence depends on the belief that cloud-native controls are superior. Does your platform validate the 'Cloud Provider' side of the debate (that their controls are enough), or does the fact that you exist prove the 'Third-Party' side (that native interfaces aren't enough)?</li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation">A key argument against native controls is an AWS WAF and a Google Cloud Armor don't behave the same way. If your tool manages native controls across multi-cloud, how do you handle the 'lowest common denominator' problem? Do you dumb down the policy to fit all clouds, or do you expose the unique complexity of each one?</li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation">GuardDuty and SCC produce similar but meaningfully different results. How do you abstract across that so an analyst or IR team isn't having to dig into the exact meaning of the different JSON fields in their output?</li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation">We often say native tools are 'good enough' for 80% of use cases but lack the depth of specialized third-party vendors (like a dedicated CNAPP or DLP). By betting your company on orchestrating native controls, are you effectively betting that 'good enough' is the future of the market? What happens when a customer needs a feature that the CSP hasn't built yet?</li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation">What fraction of your users are taking this from a "I'm 80% this one cloud, I need great coverage there and good enough elsewhere" vs "I'm truly multi-cloud" or even scarier "I have a workload that is active spanning clouds"? </li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation">Do your customers push you towards helping with the kinds of SaaS platforms that SSPM vendors cover?</li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation">If AWS and Google Cloud suddenly decided to make their native security UIs perfect and unified tomorrow, would your company cease to exist? Or is the complexity of the cloud strictly increasing, guaranteeing you job security forever?</li> </ul> <p dir="ltr">Related:</p> <ul> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation"><a href= "https://youtu.be/QMXFmNjA6B0">Video version</a></li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation"><a href= "https://cloud.withgoogle.com/cloudsecurity/podcast/ep186-cloud-security-tools-trust-the-cloud-provider-or-go-third-party-an-epic-debate-anton-vs-tim/"> EP186 Cloud Security Tools: Trust the Cloud Provider or Go Third-Party? An Epic Debate, Anton vs Tim</a></li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation"><a href= "https://cloud.withgoogle.com/cloudsecurity/podcast/ep160-dont-cloud-your-judgement-security-and-cloud-migration-again/"> EP160 Don't Cloud Your Judgement: Security and Cloud Migration, Again!</a></li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation"><a href= "https://medium.com/anton-on-security/the-great-cloud-security-debate-csp-vs-third-party-security-tools-6563e3dc6ac9"> The Great Cloud Security Debate: CSP vs. Third-Party Security Tools</a></li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation"><a href= "https://native.security/blog">native.security blog</a></li> </ul>]]></description>

      <title>EP270 The Convenience Tax: Why We Keep Failing at Supply Chain Security</title>
      <itunes:title>EP270 The Convenience Tax: Why We Keep Failing at Supply Chain Security</itunes:title>
      <pubDate>Mon, 06 Apr 2026 14:11:00 +0000</pubDate>
      <guid isPermaLink="false"><![CDATA[abacdbcf-3848-41a0-a408-36947c339a03]]></guid>
      <link><![CDATA[https://cloudsecuritypodcast.libsyn.com/ep270-the-convenience-tax-why-we-keep-failing-at-supply-chain-security]]></link>
      <description><![CDATA[<p dir="ltr">Guest:</p> <ul> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation"><a href= "https://www.linkedin.com/in/danlorenc/">Dan Lorenc</a>, Founder / CEO, <a href="https://www.chainguard.dev/">Chainguard</a></li> </ul> <p dir="ltr">Topics:</p> <ul> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation">We just saw a security tool (Trivy) get used to pop an AI infrastructure tool (LiteLLM) to eventually pop end users. Have we reached the point where our security tooling is actually our largest unmanaged attack surface? </li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation">Why now? Software supply chain security had the perennial vibe of "not top concern" for most organizations, right?</li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation">TeamPCP pushed malicious code to existing GitHub tags. We've been screaming about pinning versions to SHAs for years, but clearly, nobody is listening. Is it time to admit that 'convenience' is the primary enemy of supply chain security?</li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation">The Axios incident showed a victim compromised in under two minutes. In a world of auto-updating dependencies, is the concept of a human-in-the-loop for software updates officially dead, or do we need to look very hard at version pinning and such?</li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation">With XZ Utils case, we saw a long-game social engineering attack. Beyond just 'watching npm closely,' what are the realistic architectural safeguards for an org that knows they can't audit every line of an update?</li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation">We've spent the last three years talking about SBOMs (Software Bill of Materials) like they were a pill for supply chain health. But if the scanner producing the SBOM is the one that's compromised, isn't the SBOM just a signed receipt for your own house being on fire? </li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation">What is the one practical thing they can do to ensure their CI/CD isn't a credential-exfiltration-as-a-service platform?</li> </ul> <p dir="ltr">Resources:</p> <ul> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation"><a href= "https://youtu.be/zOhq4OEmd_o">Video version</a></li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation"><a href= "https://cloud.google.com/blog/topics/threat-intelligence/north-korea-threat-actor-targets-axios-npm-package"> North Korea-Nexus Threat Actor Compromises Widely Used Axios NPM Package in Supply Chain Attack</a></li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation"><a href= "https://cloud.withgoogle.com/cloudsecurity/podcast/ep100-2022-accelerate-state-of-devops-report-and-software-supply-chain-security/"> EP100 2022 Accelerate State of DevOps Report and Software Supply Chain Security</a></li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation"><a href= "https://cloud.withgoogle.com/cloudsecurity/podcast/ep116-sboms-a-step-towards-a-more-secure-software-supply-chain/"> EP116 SBOMs: A Step Towards a More Secure Software Supply Chain</a></li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation"><a href= "https://cloud.withgoogle.com/cloudsecurity/podcast/ep226-ai-supply-chain-security-old-lessons-new-poisons-and-agentic-dreams/"> EP226 AI Supply Chain Security: Old Lessons, New Poisons, and Agentic Dreams</a></li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation"><a href= "https://cloud.withgoogle.com/cloudsecurity/podcast/linking-up-the-pieces-software-supply-chain-security-at-google-and-beyond/"> EP24 Linking Up The Pieces: Software Supply Chain Security at Google and Beyond</a></li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation"><a href= "https://mattlevine.co/work">Matt Levine blog</a></li> </ul>]]></description>
      
      <content:encoded><![CDATA[<p dir="ltr">Guest:</p> <ul> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation"><a href= "https://www.linkedin.com/in/danlorenc/">Dan Lorenc</a>, Founder / CEO, <a href="https://www.chainguard.dev/">Chainguard</a></li> </ul> <p dir="ltr">Topics:</p> <ul> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation">We just saw a security tool (Trivy) get used to pop an AI infrastructure tool (LiteLLM) to eventually pop end users. Have we reached the point where our security tooling is actually our largest unmanaged attack surface? </li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation">Why now? Software supply chain security had the perennial vibe of "not top concern" for most organizations, right?</li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation">TeamPCP pushed malicious code to existing GitHub tags. We've been screaming about pinning versions to SHAs for years, but clearly, nobody is listening. Is it time to admit that 'convenience' is the primary enemy of supply chain security?</li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation">The Axios incident showed a victim compromised in under two minutes. In a world of auto-updating dependencies, is the concept of a human-in-the-loop for software updates officially dead, or do we need to look very hard at version pinning and such?</li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation">With XZ Utils case, we saw a long-game social engineering attack. Beyond just 'watching npm closely,' what are the realistic architectural safeguards for an org that knows they can't audit every line of an update?</li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation">We've spent the last three years talking about SBOMs (Software Bill of Materials) like they were a pill for supply chain health. But if the scanner producing the SBOM is the one that's compromised, isn't the SBOM just a signed receipt for your own house being on fire? </li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation">What is the one practical thing they can do to ensure their CI/CD isn't a credential-exfiltration-as-a-service platform?</li> </ul> <p dir="ltr">Resources:</p> <ul> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation"><a href= "https://youtu.be/zOhq4OEmd_o">Video version</a></li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation"><a href= "https://cloud.google.com/blog/topics/threat-intelligence/north-korea-threat-actor-targets-axios-npm-package"> North Korea-Nexus Threat Actor Compromises Widely Used Axios NPM Package in Supply Chain Attack</a></li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation"><a href= "https://cloud.withgoogle.com/cloudsecurity/podcast/ep100-2022-accelerate-state-of-devops-report-and-software-supply-chain-security/"> EP100 2022 Accelerate State of DevOps Report and Software Supply Chain Security</a></li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation"><a href= "https://cloud.withgoogle.com/cloudsecurity/podcast/ep116-sboms-a-step-towards-a-more-secure-software-supply-chain/"> EP116 SBOMs: A Step Towards a More Secure Software Supply Chain</a></li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation"><a href= "https://cloud.withgoogle.com/cloudsecurity/podcast/ep226-ai-supply-chain-security-old-lessons-new-poisons-and-agentic-dreams/"> EP226 AI Supply Chain Security: Old Lessons, New Poisons, and Agentic Dreams</a></li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation"><a href= "https://cloud.withgoogle.com/cloudsecurity/podcast/linking-up-the-pieces-software-supply-chain-security-at-google-and-beyond/"> EP24 Linking Up The Pieces: Software Supply Chain Security at Google and Beyond</a></li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation"><a href= "https://mattlevine.co/work">Matt Levine blog</a></li> </ul>]]></content:encoded>

      <description><![CDATA[<p dir="ltr">Guest:</p> <ul> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation"><a href= "https://www.linkedin.com/in/raffy/">Raffael Marty</a>, Operating Advisor, a SIEM legend since 1999</li> </ul> <p dir="ltr">Topics:</p> <ul> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation">You argue that declaring existing SIEM being obsolete is a "marketing slogan" rather than a true thesis. What is the real pain point and the actual gap in traditional SIEMs as opposed to the more sensational claims?</li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation">You highlight that "correlation, state, timelines, and real-time detection require locality," making centralization a necessary trade-off. Can a truly federated or decoupled SIEM architecture achieve the same fidelity and real-time performance for complex, stateful detections as a centralized one?</li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation">You call the rise of independent security data pipelines the "SIEM Trojan Horse." How quickly is this abstraction layer turning SIEM into a "swappable" component, and what should SIEM vendors have done differently years ago to prevent this market from existing?</li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation">This "AI SOC" thing, is this even real? Is AI in a SOC a better label? Do you think major SIEM vendors will own this very soon, like they did with UEBA and SOAR?</li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation">If volume-based pricing is flawed because it penalizes good security hygiene, what is a better SIEM pricing model that fairly addresses compute, enrichment, and retention costs without just shifting the volume cost to unpredictable query charges?</li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation">You question the idea that startups can find a better way to release detection rules than large vendors with significant content teams.       <title>EP264  Measuring Your (Agentic) SOC: Two Security Leaders Walk into a Podcast</title>
      <itunes:title>EP264  Measuring Your (Agentic) SOC: Two Security Leaders Walk into a Podcast</itunes:title>
      <pubDate>Mon, 23 Feb 2026 15:02:00 +0000</pubDate>
      <guid isPermaLink="false"><![CDATA[fc4943d2-856b-4257-b7a7-3e744c4675a7]]></guid>
      <link><![CDATA[https://cloudsecuritypodcast.libsyn.com/ep264-measuring-your-agentic-soc-two-security-leaders-walk-into-a-podcast]]></link>
      <description><![CDATA[<p dir="ltr">Guests:</p> <ul> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation"><a href= "https://www.linkedin.com/in/apabst/">Alexander  Pabst</a>, Global Deputy CISO, Allianz SE</li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation"><a href= "https://www.linkedin.com/in/michael-sinno-a83b60/">Michael Sinno</a>, Director of D&R, Google</li> </ul> <p dir="ltr">Topics:</p> <ul> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation">We've spent decades obsessed with MTTD (Mean Time to Detect) and MTTR (Mean Time to Respond). As AI agents begin to handle the bulk of triage at machine speed, do these metrics become "vanity metrics"? If an AI resolves an alert in seconds, does measuring the "mean" still tell us anything about the health of our security program, or should we be looking at "Time to Context" instead?</li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation">You mentioned the Maturity Triangle. Can you walk us through that framework? Specifically, how does AI change the balance between the three points of that triangle—is it shifting us from a "People-heavy" model to something more "Engineering-led," and where does the "Measurement" piece sit?</li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation">Google is famous for its <a href= "https://cloud.google.com/blog/products/identity-security/modernizing-soc-introducing-autonomic-security-operations"> "Engineering-led" approach to D&R</a>. How is Google currently measuring the success of its own internal D&R program? Specifically, how are you quantifying "Toil Reduction"? Are we measuring how many hours we saved, or are we measuring the complexity of the threats our humans are now free to hunt?</li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation">Toil reduction is a laudable goal for the team members, what are the metrics we track and report up to document the overall improvement in D&R for Google's board?</li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation">When you talk to your board about the success of AI in your security program, what are the 2 or 3 "Golden Metrics" that actually move the needle for them? How do you prove that an AI-driven SOC is actually better, not just faster?</li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation">We often talk about AI as an "assistant," but we're moving toward Agentic SOCs. How should organizations measure the "unit economics" of their SOC? Should we be tracking the ratio of AI-handled vs. Human-handled incidents, and at what point does a high AI-handle rate become a risk rather than a success?</li> </ul> <p dir="ltr">Resources:</p> <ul> Fidelity, and Measuring Success</a></li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation"><a href= "https://cloud.withgoogle.com/cloudsecurity/podcast/ep238-google-lessons-for-using-ai-agents-for-securing-our-enterprise/"> EP238 Google Lessons for Using AI Agents for Securing Our Enterprise</a></li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation"><a href= "https://cloud.withgoogle.com/cloudsecurity/podcast/ep91-hacking-google-op-aurora-and-insider-threat-at-google/"> EP91 "Hacking Google", Op Aurora and Insider Threat at Google</a></li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation"><a href= "https://cloud.withgoogle.com/cloudsecurity/podcast/ep236-accelerated-siem-journey-a-soc-leaders-playbook-for-modernization-and-ai/"> EP236 Accelerated SIEM Journey: A SOC Leader's Playbook for Also, define "AI agent" please.</li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation">What are your production use cases for AI and AI agents in your SOC?</li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation">What are your overall SOC metrics and how does the agentic AI part play into that?</li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation">It's one thing to ask a team "hey what did y'all do last week" and get a good report - how are you measuring the agentic parts of your SOC?</li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation">How are you thinking about what comes next once AI is automatically writing good (!) rules for your team out of research blog posts and TI papers? </li> </ul> <p dir="ltr">Resources:</p> <ul> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation"><a href= "https://youtu.be/KJmZ6tWDMV0">Video version</a></li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation"><a href= "https://www.linkedin.com/pulse/agentic-ai-soc-build-vs-buy-lessons-mustapha-kebbeh-msgye/"> Agentic AI in the SOC: Build vs Buy Lessons</a></li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation"><a href= "https://cloud.withgoogle.com/cloudsecurity/podcast/ep255-separating-hype-from-hazard-the-truth-about-autonomous-ai-hacking/"> EP255 Separating Hype from Hazard: The Truth About Autonomous AI Hacking</a></li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation"><a href= "https://cloud.withgoogle.com/cloudsecurity/podcast/ep256-rewiring-democracy-hacking-trust-bruce-schneier-on-the-ai-offense-defense-balance/"> EP256 Rewiring Democracy & Hacking Trust: Bruce Schneier on the AI Offense-Defense Balance</a></li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation"><a href= "https://cloud.withgoogle.com/cloudsecurity/podcast/ep252-the-agentic-soc-reality-governing-ai-agents-data-fidelity-and-measuring-success/"> EP252 The Agentic SOC Reality: Governing AI Agents, Data Fidelity, and Measuring Success</a></li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation"><a href= "https://cloud.withgoogle.com/cloudsecurity/podcast/ep236-accelerated-siem-journey-a-soc-leaders-playbook-for-modernization-and-ai/"> EP236 Accelerated SIEM Journey: A SOC Leader's Playbook for Modernization and AI</a></li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation"><a href= "https://cloud.withgoogle.com/cloudsecurity/podcast/ep242-the-ai-soc-is-this-the-automation-weve-been-waiting-for/"> EP242 The AI SOC: Is This The Automation We've Been Waiting For?</a></li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation"><a href= "https://cloud.google.com/resources/boost-your-cloud-skills-with-google"> Google Cloud Skill Boost</a></li> </ul> <p> </p>]]></content:encoded>

      <title>EP258 Why Your Security Strategy Needs an Immune System, Not a Fortress with Royal Hansen</title>
      <itunes:title>EP258 Why Your Security Strategy Needs an Immune System, Not a Fortress with Royal Hansen</itunes:title>
      <pubDate>Mon, 12 Jan 2026 15:11:00 +0000</pubDate>
      <guid isPermaLink="false"><![CDATA[570203d1-7dd7-40e9-a2d1-4d604355b53c]]></guid>
      <link><![CDATA[https://cloudsecuritypodcast.libsyn.com/ep258-why-your-security-strategy-needs-an-immune-system-not-a-fortress-with-royal-hansen]]></link>
      <description><![CDATA[<p dir="ltr">Guest:</p> <ul> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation"><a href= "https://www.linkedin.com/in/royal-hansen-989858/">Royal Hansen</a>, VP of Engineering at Google, former CISO of Alphabet</li> </ul> <p dir="ltr">Topics:</p> <ul> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation">The "God-Like Designer" Fallacy: You've argued that we need to move away from the "God-like designer" model of security—where we pre-calculate every risk like building a bridge—and towards a biological model. Can you explain why that old engineering mindset is becoming risky in today's cloud and AI environments?</li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation">Resilience vs. Robustness: In your view, what is the practical difference between a robust system (like a fortress that eventually breaks) and a resilient system (like an immune system)? How does a CISO start shifting their team's focus from creating the former to nurturing the latter?</li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation">Securing the Unknown: We're entering an era where <a href= "https://security.googlecloudcommunity.com/ciso-blog-77/10-tips-for-governing-ai-agents-6081"> AI agents</a> will call other agents, creating pathways we never explicitly designed. If we can't predict these interactions, how can we possibly secure them? What does "emergent security" look like in practice?</li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation">Primitives for Agents: You mentioned the need for new "biological primitives" for these agents—things like time-bound access or inherent throttling. Are these just new names for old concepts like Zero Trust, or is there something different about how we need to apply them to AI?</li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation">The Compliance Friction: There's a massive tension between this dynamic, probabilistic reality and the static, checklist-based world of many compliance regimes. How do you, as a leader, bridge that gap? How do you convince an auditor or a board that a "probabilistic" approach doesn't just mean "we don't know for sure"?</li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation"> "Safe" Failures: How can organizations get comfortable with the idea of designing for allowable failure in their subsystems, rather than striving for 100% uptime and security everywhere?</li> </ul> <p dir="ltr">Resources:</p> <ul> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation"><a href= "https://youtu.be/1RfrEfBrjYg">Video version</a></li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation"><a href= "https://cloud.withgoogle.com/cloudsecurity/podcast/ep189-how-google-does-security-programs-at-scale-ciso-insights/"> EP189 How Google Does Security Programs at Scale: CISO Insights</a></li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation"><a href= "https://cloud.google.com/blog/products/identity-security/cloud-ciso-perspectives-our-big-sleep-agent-makes-big-leap"> BigSleep</a> and <a href= "https://deepmind.google/blog/introducing-codemender-an-ai-agent-for-code-security/"> CodeMender</a> agents</li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation"><a href= "https://www.amazon.com/Chasing-Rabbit-Outdistance-Competition-Christensen/dp/0071499881"> "Chasing the Rabbit"</a> book  </li> <li><a href= "https://www.amazon.com/dp/0226826686?ref_=ppx_hzsearch_conn_dt_b_fed_asin_title_27"> "How Life Works: A User's Guide to the New Biology"</a> book</li> </ul>]]></description>
      
      <content:encoded><![CDATA[<p dir="ltr">Guest:</p> <ul> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation"><a href= "https://www.linkedin.com/in/royal-hansen-989858/">Royal Hansen</a>, VP of Engineering at Google, former CISO of Alphabet</li> </ul> <p dir="ltr">Topics:</p> <ul> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation">The "God-Like Designer" Fallacy: You've argued that we need to move away from the "God-like designer" model of security—where we pre-calculate every risk like building a bridge—and towards a biological model.       <title>EP255 Separating Hype from Hazard: The Truth About Autonomous AI Hacking</title>
      <itunes:title>EP255 Separating Hype from Hazard: The Truth About Autonomous AI Hacking</itunes:title>
      <pubDate>Mon, 08 Dec 2025 15:11:00 +0000</pubDate>
      <guid isPermaLink="false"><![CDATA[933df24c-b411-4e10-8fe4-7c5bd01ca3f2]]></guid>
      <link><![CDATA[https://cloudsecuritypodcast.libsyn.com/ep255-separating-hype-from-hazard-the-truth-about-autonomous-ai-hacking]]></link>
      <description><![CDATA[<p dir="ltr">Guest:</p> <ul> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation"><a href= "https://www.linkedin.com/in/argvee/">Heather Adkins</a>, VP of Security Engineering, Google</li> </ul> <p dir="ltr">Topic:</p> <ul> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation">The term "AI Hacking Singularity" sounds like pure sci-fi, yet you and some other very credible folks <a href= "https://www.csoonline.com/article/4069075/autonomous-ai-hacking-and-the-future-of-cybersecurity.html"> are using it to</a> describe an imminent threat. How much of this is hyperbole to shock the complacent, and how much is based on actual, observed capabilities today? </li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation">Can autonomous AI agents really achieve that "exploit - at - machine - velocity" without human intervention for the zero-day discovery phase?</li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation">On the other hand, why may it actually not happen?</li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation">When we talk about autonomous AI attack platforms, are we talking about highly resourced nation-states and top-tier criminal groups, or will this capability truly be accessible to the average threat actor within the next 6-12 months? What's the "Metasploit" equivalent for AI-powered exploitation that will be ubiquitous? </li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation">Can you paint a realistic picture of the worst-case scenario that autonomous AI hacking enables? Is it a complete breakdown of patch cycles, a global infrastructure collapse, or something worse?</li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation">If attackers are operating at "machine speed," the human defender is fundamentally outmatched. Is there a genuine "AI-to-AI" counter-tactic that doesn't just devolve into an infinite arms race? Or can we counter without AI at all?</li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation">Given that AI can expedite vulnerability discovery, how does this amplified threat vector impact the software supply chain? If a dependency is compromised within minutes of a new vulnerability being created, does this force the industry to completely abandon the open-source model, or does it demand a radical, real-time security scanning and patching system that only a handful of tech giants can afford?</li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation">Are current proposed regulations, like those focusing on model safety or disclosure, even targeting the right problem? </li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation">If the real danger is the combinatorial speed of autonomous attack agents, what simple, impactful policy change should world governments prioritize right now?</li> </ul> <p dir="ltr">Resources:</p> <ul> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation"><a href= "https://www.csoonline.com/article/4069075/autonomous-ai-hacking-and-the-future-of-cybersecurity.html"> "Autonomous AI hacking and the future of cybersecurity"</a> article</li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation"><a href= "https://cloud.withgoogle.com/cloudsecurity/podcast/security-operations-reliability-and-securing-google-with-heather-adkins/"> EP20 Security Operations, Reliability, and Securing Google with Heather Adkins</a></li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation"><a href= "https://deepmind.google/blog/introducing-codemender-an-ai-agent-for-code-security/"> Introducing CodeMender: an AI agent for code security</a></li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation"><a href= "https://cloud.withgoogle.com/cloudsecurity/podcast/ep251-beyond-fancy-scripts-can-ai-red-teaming-find-truly-novel-attacks/"> EP251 Beyond Fancy Scripts: Can AI Red Teaming Find Truly Novel Attacks?</a></li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation"><a href= "https://danielmiessler.com/">Daniel Miessler site</a> and <a href= "https://podcasts.apple.com/us/podcast/unsupervised-learning/id1099711235"> podcast</a></li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation"><a href= "https://cloud.google.com/blog/transform/how-saif-can-accelerate-secure-ai-experiments-infographic/"> "How SAIF can accelerate secure AI experiments"</a> blog</li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation"><a href= "https://security.googlecloudcommunity.com/ciso-blog-77/staying-on-top-of-ai-developments-4060"> "Staying on top of AI Developments"</a> blog</li> </ul>]]></description>

      <title>EP254 Escaping 1990s Vulnerability Management: From Unauthenticated Scans to AI-Driven Mitigation</title>
      <itunes:title>EP254 Escaping 1990s Vulnerability Management: From Unauthenticated Scans to AI-Driven Mitigation</itunes:title>
      <pubDate>Mon, 01 Dec 2025 19:24:00 +0000</pubDate>
      <guid isPermaLink="false"><![CDATA[6e5fe549-400e-4c2d-93b2-1a4d9d3d6c1a]]></guid>
      <link><![CDATA[https://cloudsecuritypodcast.libsyn.com/ep254-escaping-1990s-vulnerability-management-from-unauthenticated-scans-to-ai-driven-mitigation]]></link>
      <description><![CDATA[<p dir="ltr">Guest:</p> <ul> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation"><a href= "https://www.linkedin.com/in/caleb-hoch/">Caleb Hoch</a>, Consulting Manager on Security Transformation Team, Mandiant, Google Cloud</li> </ul> <p dir="ltr">Topics:</p> <ul> <li>How has vulnerability management (VM) evolved beyond basic scanning and reporting, and what are the biggest gaps between modern practices and what organizations are actually doing?</li> <li>Why are so many organizations stuck with 1990s VM practices?</li> <li>Why mitigation planning is still hard for so many?</li> <li>Why do many organizations, including large ones, still rely on unauthenticated scans despite the known importance of authenticated scanning for accurate results?</li> <li>What constitutes a "gold standard" vulnerability prioritization process in 2025 that moves beyond CVSS scores to incorporate threat intelligence, asset criticality, and other contextual factors?</li> <li>What are the primary human and organizational challenges in vulnerability management, and how can issues like unclear governance, lack of accountability, and fear of system crashes be overcome?</li> <li>How is AI impacting vulnerability management, and does the shift to cloud environments fundamentally change VM practices?</li> </ul> <p dir="ltr">Resources:</p> <ul> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation"><a href= "https://cloud.withgoogle.com/cloudsecurity/podcast/ep109-how-google-does-vulnerability-management-the-not-so-secret-secrets/"> EP109 How Google Does Vulnerability Management: The Not So Secret Secrets!</a></li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation"><a href=       <title>EP251 Beyond Fancy Scripts: Can AI Red Teaming Find Truly Novel Attacks?</title>
      <itunes:title>EP251 Beyond Fancy Scripts: Can AI Red Teaming Find Truly Novel Attacks?</itunes:title>
      <pubDate>Mon, 10 Nov 2025 15:11:00 +0000</pubDate>
      <guid isPermaLink="false"><![CDATA[654926c6-211d-4b8d-a3a1-38bb9367eb34]]></guid>
      <link><![CDATA[https://cloudsecuritypodcast.libsyn.com/ep251-beyond-fancy-scripts-can-ai-red-teaming-find-truly-novel-attacks]]></link>
      <description><![CDATA[<p dir="ltr">Guest:</p> <ul> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation"><a href= "https://www.linkedin.com/in/adversariel/">Ari Herbert-Voss</a>, CEO at <a href="https://www.runsybil.com/">RunSybil</a></li> </ul> <p dir="ltr">Topics:</p> <ul> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation">The market already has Breach and Attack Simulation (BAS), for testing known TTPs. You're calling this 'AI-powered' red teaming. Is this just a fancy LLM stringing together known attacks, or is there a genuine agent here that can discover a truly novel attack path that a human hasn't scripted for it?</li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation">Let's talk about the 'so what?' problem. Pentest reports are famous for becoming shelf-ware. How do you turn a complex AI finding into an actionable ticket for a developer, and more importantly, how do you help a CISO decide which of the thousand 'criticals' to actually fix first?</li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation">You're asking customers to unleash a 'hacker AI' in their production environment. That's terrifying. What are the 'do no harm' guardrails? How do you guarantee your AI won't accidentally rm -rf a critical server or cause a denial of service while it's 'exploring'?</li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation">You mentioned the AI is particularly good at finding authentication bugs. Why that specific category? What's the secret sauce there, and what's the reaction from customers when you show them those types of flaws?</li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation">Is this AI meant to replace a human red teamer, or make them better? Does it automate the boring stuff so experts can focus on creative business logic attacks, or is the ultimate goal to automate the entire red team function away?</li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation">So, is this just about finding holes, or are you closing the loop for the blue team? Can the attack paths your AI finds be automatically translated into high-fidelity detection rules? Is the end goal a continuous purple team engine that's constantly training our defenses?</li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation">Also, what about fixing? What makes your findings more fixable?</li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation">What will happen to red team testing in 2-3 years if this technology gets better?</li> </ul> <p dir="ltr">Resource:</p> <ul> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation"><a href= "https://www.zetter-zeroday.com/about/">Kim Zetter Zero Day blog</a></li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation"><a href= "https://cloud.withgoogle.com/cloudsecurity/podcast/ep230-ai-red-teaming-surprises-strategies-and-lessons-from-google/"> EP230 AI Red Teaming: Surprises, Strategies, and Lessons from Google</a></li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation"><a href= "https://cloud.withgoogle.com/cloudsecurity/podcast/ep217-red-teaming-ai-uncovering-surprises-facing-new-threats-and-the-same-old-mistakes/"> EP217 Red Teaming AI: Uncovering Surprises, Facing New Threats, and the Same Old Mistakes?</a></li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation"><a href= "https://cloud.withgoogle.com/cloudsecurity/podcast/ep68-how-we-attack-ai-learn-more-at-our-rsa-panel/"> EP68 How We Attack AI? Learn More at Our RSA Panel!</a></li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation"><a href= "https://cloud.withgoogle.com/cloudsecurity/podcast/ep71-attacking-google-to-defend-google-how-google-does-red-team/"> EP71 Attacking Google to Defend Google: How Google Does Red Team</a></li> </ul> <p> </p>]]></description>
      
      <content:encoded><![CDATA[<p dir="ltr">Guest:</p> <ul> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation"><a href= "https://www.linkedin.com/in/adversariel/">Ari Herbert-Voss</a>, CEO at <a href="https://www.runsybil.com/">RunSybil</a></li> </ul> <p dir="ltr">Topics:</p> <ul> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation">The market already has Breach and Attack Simulation (BAS), for testing known TTPs. You're calling this 'AI-powered' red teaming. Is this just a fancy LLM stringing together known attacks, or is there a genuine agent here that can discover a truly novel attack path that a human hasn't scripted for it?</li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation">Let's talk about the 'so what?' problem. Pentest reports are famous for becoming shelf-ware. How do you turn a complex AI finding into an actionable ticket for a developer, and more importantly, how do you help a CISO decide which of the thousand 'criticals' to actually fix first?</li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation">You're asking customers to unleash a 'hacker AI' in their production environment. That's terrifying. What are the 'do no harm' guardrails? How do you guarantee your AI won't accidentally rm -rf a critical server or cause a denial of service while it's 'exploring'?</li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation">You mentioned the AI is particularly good at finding authentication bugs. Why that specific category? What's the secret sauce there, and what's the reaction from customers when you show them those types of flaws?</li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation">Is this AI meant to replace a human red teamer, or make them better? Does it automate the boring stuff so experts can focus on creative business logic attacks, or is the ultimate goal to automate the entire red team function away?</li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation">So, is this just about finding holes, or are you closing the loop for the blue team? Can the attack paths your AI finds be automatically translated into high-fidelity detection rules? Is the end goal a continuous purple team engine that's constantly training our defenses?</li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation">Also, what about fixing? What makes your findings more fixable?</li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation">What will happen to red team testing in 2-3 years if this technology gets better?</li> </ul> <p dir="ltr">Resource:</p> <ul> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation"><a href= "https://www.zetter-zeroday.com/about/">Kim Zetter Zero Day blog</a></li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation"><a href= "https://cloud.withgoogle.com/cloudsecurity/podcast/ep230-ai-red-teaming-surprises-strategies-and-lessons-from-google/"> EP230 AI Red Teaming: Surprises, Strategies, and Lessons from Google</a></li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation"><a href= "https://cloud.withgoogle.com/cloudsecurity/podcast/ep217-red-teaming-ai-uncovering-surprises-facing-new-threats-and-the-same-old-mistakes/"> EP217 Red Teaming AI: Uncovering Surprises, Facing New Threats, and the Same Old Mistakes?</a></li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation"><a href= "https://cloud.withgoogle.com/cloudsecurity/podcast/ep68-how-we-attack-ai-learn-more-at-our-rsa-panel/"> EP68 How We Attack AI? Learn More at Our RSA Panel!</a></li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation"><a href= "https://cloud.withgoogle.com/cloudsecurity/podcast/ep71-attacking-google-to-defend-google-how-google-does-red-team/"> EP71 Attacking Google to Defend Google: How Google Does Red Team</a></li> </ul> <p> </p>]]></content:encoded>

      <title>EP241 From Black Box to Building Blocks:  More Modern Detection Engineering Lessons from Google</title>
      <itunes:title>EP241 From Black Box to Building Blocks:  More Modern Detection Engineering Lessons from Google</itunes:title>
      <pubDate>Mon, 01 Sep 2025 14:11:00 +0000</pubDate>
      <guid isPermaLink="false"><![CDATA[e09b2a35-a65c-48fb-9e12-6a5a5a437aca]]></guid>

      <description><![CDATA[<p dir="ltr">Guest:</p> <ul> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation"><a href= "mailto:rickcorrea@google.com"><span data-rich-links= "{"per_n":"Rick Correa","per_e":"rickcorrea@google.com","type":"person"}"> Rick Correa</span></a>,Uber TL Google SecOps, Google Cloud</li> </ul> <p dir="ltr">Topics:</p> <ul> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation">On the 3rd anniversary of Curated Detections, you've grown from 70 rules to over 4700. Can you walk us through that journey? What were some of the key inflection points and what have been the biggest lessons learned in scaling a detection portfolio so massively?</li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation">Historically the <a href= "https://cloud.google.com/chronicle/docs/detection/curated-detections"> SecOps Curated Detection</a> content was opaque, which led to, understandably, a bit of customer friction. We've recently made nearly all of that content transparent and editable by users. What were the challenges in that transition?</li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation">You make a distinction between "Detection-as-Code" and a more mature "Software Engineering" paradigm. What gets better for a security team when they move beyond just version control and a CI/CD pipeline and start incorporating things like unit testing, readability reviews, and performance testing for their detections?</li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation">The idea of a "Goldilocks Zone" for detections is intriguing – not too many, not too few. How do you find that balance, and what are the metrics that matter when measuring the effectiveness of a detection program? You mentioned customer feedback is important, but a <a href= "https://medium.com/@tam.tamanna18/understanding-the-confusion-matrix-and-its-applications-3a1c33d799af"> confusion matrix</a> isn't possible, why is that?</li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation">You talk about enabling customers to use your "building blocks" to create their own detections. Can you give us a practical example of how a customer might use a building block for something like detecting VPN and Tor traffic to augment their security?</li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation">You have started using LLMs for reviewing the explainability of human-generated metadata. Can you expand on that? What have you found are the ripe areas for AI in detection engineering, and can you share any anecdotes of where AI has succeeded and where it has failed?</li> </ul> <p dir="ltr"><br />    Resources</p> <ul> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation"><a href= "https://cloud.withgoogle.com/cloudsecurity/podcast/ep197-siem-decoupled-or-not-and-security-data-lakes-a-google-secops-perspective/"> EP197 SIEM (Decoupled or Not), and Security Data Lakes: A Google SecOps Perspective</a></li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation"><a href= "https://cloud.withgoogle.com/cloudsecurity/podcast/ep231-beyond-the-buzzword-practical-detection-as-code-in-the-enterprise/"> EP231 Beyond the Buzzword: Practical Detection as Code in the Enterprise</a></li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation"><a href= "https://cloud.withgoogle.com/cloudsecurity/podcast/ep181-detection-engineering-deep-dive-from-career-paths-to-scaling-soc-teams/"> EP181 Detection Engineering Deep Dive: From Career Paths to Scaling SOC Teams</a></li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation"><a href= "https://cloud.withgoogle.com/cloudsecurity/podcast/ep139-what-is-chronicle-beyond-xdr-and-into-the-next-generation-of-security-operations/"> EP139 What is Chronicle? What lessons do you have for other security leaders preparing their teams for the AI in SOC transition? </li> </ul> <p dir="ltr">Resources:</p> <ul> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation"><a href= "https://cloud.withgoogle.com/cloudsecurity/podcast/ep234-the-siem-paradox-logs-lies-and-failing-to-detect/"> EP234 The SIEM Paradox: Logs, Lies, and Failing to Detect</a></li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation"><a href= "https://cloud.withgoogle.com/cloudsecurity/podcast/ep197-siem-decoupled-or-not-and-security-data-lakes-a-google-secops-perspective/"> EP197 SIEM (Decoupled or Not), and Security Data Lakes: A Google SecOps Perspective</a></li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation"><a href= "https://cloud.withgoogle.com/cloudsecurity/podcast/ep231-beyond-the-buzzword-practical-detection-as-code-in-the-enterprise/"> EP231 Beyond the Buzzword: Practical Detection as Code in the Enterprise</a></li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation"><a href= "https://cloud.withgoogle.com/cloudsecurity/podcast/ep184-one-week-siem-migration-fact-or-fiction/"> EP184 One Week SIEM Migration: Fact or Fiction?</a></li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation"><a href= "https://cloud.withgoogle.com/cloudsecurity/podcast/ep125-will-siem-ever-die-siem-lessons-from-the-past-for-the-future/"> EP125 Will SIEM Ever Die: SIEM Lessons from the Past for the Future</a></li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation"><a href= "https://cloud.withgoogle.com/cloudsecurity/podcast/ep223-ai-addressable-not-ai-solvable-reflections-from-rsa-2025/"> EP223 AI Addressable, Not AI Solvable: Reflections from RSA 2025</a></li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation"><a href= "https://medium.com/anton-on-security/maverick-scorched-earth-siem-migration-ftw-8a1467cb5501"> "Maverick" — Scorched Earth SIEM Migration FTW!</a> blog</li> <li><a href="https://www.hackthebox.com/">"Hack the box"</a> site</li> </ul>]]></content:encoded>

      <title>EP229 Beyond the Hype: Debunking Cloud Breach Myths (and What DBIR Says Now)</title>
      <itunes:title>EP229 Beyond the Hype: Debunking Cloud Breach Myths (and What DBIR Says Now)</itunes:title>
      <pubDate>Mon, 09 Jun 2025 14:11:00 +0000</pubDate>
      <guid isPermaLink="false"><![CDATA[d01d5117-fd2f-4f89-bc04-fb540d6c4972]]></guid>
      <link><![CDATA[https://cloudsecuritypodcast.libsyn.com/ep229-beyond-the-hype-debunking-cloud-breach-myths-and-what-dbir-says-now]]></link>
      <description><![CDATA[<p dir="ltr">Guest:</p> <ul> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation"><a href= "https://www.linkedin.com/in/alexcpsec/">Alex Pinto</a>,  Associate Director of Threat Intelligence, Verizon Business, Lead the Verizon Data Breach Report</li> </ul> <p dir="ltr">Topics:</p> <ul> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation">How would you define "a cloud breach"? Is that a real (and different) thing? </li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation">Are cloud breaches just a result of leaked keys and creds?</li> <li>If customers are responsible for 99% of cloud security problems, is cloud breach really about <a href= "https://medium.com/anton-on-security/no-snow-no-flakes-pondering-cloud-security-shared-responsibility-again-10b51e4ebba3"> a customer being breached</a>?</li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation">Are misconfigurations really responsible for so many cloud security breaches? How are we <a href="https://medium.com/anton-on-security/using-cloud-securely-the-config-doom-question-36e7e9c018e2"> still failing</a> at configuration?</li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation">What parts of DBIR are not total <a href= "https://medium.com/anton-on-security/rsa-2025-ais-promise-vs-security-s-past-a-reality-check-e06deb3bd579"> "groundhog day"</a>?</li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation">Something about vuln exploitation vs credential abuse in today's breaches–what's driving the shifts we're seeing? DBIR</li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation">Are we at peak ransomware? Will ransomware be here in 20 years? Will we be here in 20 years talking about it?</li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation">How is AI changing the breach report, other than putting in hilarious footnotes about how the report is for humans to read and and is written by actual humans? </li> </ul> <p dir="ltr">Resources:</p> <ul> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation">Video (<a href= "https://www.linkedin.com/events/livefromrsacloudsecuritypodcast7320920613013901312/comments/">LinkedIn</a>, <a href="https://youtu.be/IrdVGebPpZA">YouTube</a>)</li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation"><a href= "https://www.verizon.com/business/resources/reports/dbir/">Verizon DBIR 2025</a></li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation"><a href= "https://cloud.withgoogle.com/cloudsecurity/podcast/ep222-from-post-ir-lessons-to-proactive-security-deconstructing-mandiant-m-trends/"> EP222 From Post-IR Lessons to Proactive Security: Deconstructing Mandiant M-Trends</a></li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation"><a href= "https://cloud.withgoogle.com/cloudsecurity/podcast/ep205-cybersecurity-forecast-2025-beyond-the-hype-and-into-the-reality/"> EP205 Cybersecurity Forecast 2025: Beyond the Hype and into the Reality</a></li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation"><a href= "https://cloud.withgoogle.com/cloudsecurity/podcast/ep112-threat-horizons-how-google-does-threat-intelligence/"> EP112 Threat Horizons - How Google Does Threat Intelligence</a></li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation"><a href= "https://cloud.withgoogle.com/cloudsecurity/podcast/ep223-ai-addressable-not-ai-solvable-reflections-from-rsa-2025/"> EP223 AI Addressable, Not AI Solvable: Reflections from RSA 2025</a></li> </ul> <p> </p>]]></description>

      <title>EP226 AI Supply Chain Security: Old Lessons, New Poisons, and Agentic Dreams</title>

    <item>
      <title>EP223 AI Addressable, Not AI Solvable: Reflections from RSA 2025</title>
      <itunes:title>EP223 AI Addressable, Not AI Solvable: Reflections from RSA 2025</itunes:title>
      <pubDate>Mon, 05 May 2025 14:11:00 +0000</pubDate>
      <guid isPermaLink="false"><![CDATA[a24373c6-a5e8-44f3-85d0-c7f9db4b2b97]]></guid>
      <link><![CDATA[https://cloudsecuritypodcast.libsyn.com/ep223-ai-addressable-not-ai-solvable-reflections-from-rsa-2025]]></link>
      <description><![CDATA[<p dir="ltr">Guests: </p> <ul> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation">no guests, just us in the studio</li> </ul> <p dir="ltr">Topics:</p> <ul> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation">At RSA 2025, did we see solid, measurably better outcomes from AI use in security, or mostly just "sizzle" and good ideas with potential?</li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation">Are the promises of an "AI SOC" repeating the mistakes seen with SOAR in previous years regarding fully automated security operations? Does "AI SOC" work according to RSA floor?</li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation">How realistic is the vision expressed by some [yes, really!] that AI progress could lead to technical teams, including IT and security, shrinking dramatically or even to zero in a few years?</li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation">Why do companies continue to rely on decades-old or "non-leading" security technologies, and what role does the concept of a "organizational change budget" play in this inertia?</li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation">Is being "AI Native" fundamentally better for security technologies compared to adding AI capabilities to existing platforms, or is the jury still out? Got "an AI-native SIEM"?       <title>EP219 Beyond the Buzzwords: Decoding Cyber Risk and Threat Actors in Asia Pacific</title>
      <itunes:title>EP219 Beyond the Buzzwords: Decoding Cyber Risk and Threat Actors in Asia Pacific</itunes:title>
      <pubDate>Mon, 14 Apr 2025 12:11:00 +0000</pubDate>
      <guid isPermaLink="false"><![CDATA[a0430680-6d79-4c3b-b741-fd3b257203a9]]></guid>
      <link><![CDATA[https://cloudsecuritypodcast.libsyn.com/ep219-beyond-the-buzzwords-decoding-cyber-risk-and-threat-actors-in-asia-pacific]]></link>
      <description><![CDATA[<p dir="ltr">Guest:</p> <ul> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation"><a href= "https://www.linkedin.com/in/steve-ledzian-3a12b4/">Steve Ledzian</a>, APAC CTO, Mandiant at Google Cloud</li> </ul> <p dir="ltr">Topics:</p> <ul> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation">We've seen a shift in how boards engage with cybersecurity. From your perspective, what's the most significant misconception boards still hold about cyber risk, particularly in the Asia Pacific region, and how has that impacted their decision-making?</li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation">Cybersecurity is rife with jargon. If you could eliminate or redefine one overused term, which would it be and why? How does this overloaded language specifically hinder effective communication and action in the region?</li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation">The <a href= "https://cloud.google.com/security/resources/insights/targeted-attack-lifecycle"> Mandiant Attack Lifecycle</a> is a well-known model.       <title>EP216 Ephemeral Clouds, Lasting Security: CIRA, CDR, and the Future of Cloud Investigations</title>

      <description><![CDATA[<p dir="ltr">Guest:</p> <ul> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation"><a href= "https://www.linkedin.com/in/cirninja/">James Campbell</a>, CEO, <a href="https://www.cadosecurity.com/">Cado Security</a></li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation"><a href= "https://www.linkedin.com/in/cdoman/">Chris Doman</a>, CTO, <a href="https://www.cadosecurity.com/">Cado Security</a></li> </ul> <p dir="ltr">Topics:</p> <ul> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation">Cloud Detection and Response (CDR) vs Cloud Investigation and Response Automation(<a href= "https://www.gartner.com/reviews/market/cloud-investigation-and-response-automation-cira">CIRA</a>) ... what's the story here?       <title>EP214 Reconciling the Impossible: Engineering Cloud Systems for Diverging Regulations</title>
      <itunes:title>EP214 Reconciling the Impossible: Engineering Cloud Systems for Diverging Regulations</itunes:title>
      <pubDate>Mon, 10 Mar 2025 15:11:00 +0000</pubDate>
      <guid isPermaLink="false"><![CDATA[b9e015c0-ee23-4c8b-b1d0-decb39680032]]></guid>
      <link><![CDATA[https://cloudsecuritypodcast.libsyn.com/ep214-reconciling-the-impossible-engineering-cloud-systems-for-diverging-regulations]]></link>
      <description><![CDATA[<p dir="ltr">Guest:</p> <ul> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation"><a href= "https://www.linkedin.com/in/archanaramamoorthy/">Archana Ramamoorthy</a>, Senior Director of Product Management, Google Cloud</li> </ul> <p dir="ltr">Topics:</p> <ul> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation">You are responsible for building systems that need to comply with laws that are often mutually contradictory. It seems technically impossible to do, how do you do this?</li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation">Google is not alone in being a global company with local customers and local requirements. How are we building systems that provide local compliance with global consistency in their use for customers who are similar in scale to us? </li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation">Originally, Google had global systems synchronized around the entire planet–planet scale supercompute–with atomic clocks. How did we get to regionalized approach from there? </li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation">Engineering takes a long time. How do we bring enough agility to product definition and engineering design to give our users robust foundations in our systems that also let us keep up with changing and diverging regulatory goals?</li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation">What are some of the biggest challenges you face working in the trusted cloud space?</li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation">Is there something you would like to share about being a woman leader in technology?  How did you overcome the related challenges?</li> </ul> <p dir="ltr">Resources:</p> <ul> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation"><a href= "https://youtu.be/28z2Au40UyM">Video</a></li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation"><a href= "https://www.forbes.com/sites/googlecloud/2020/07/14/compliance-without-compromise/"> "Compliance Without Compromise"</a> by Jeanette Manfra (2020, still very relevant!)</li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation"><a href= "https://www.amazon.com/Good-Great-Some-Companies-Others/dp/0066620996"> "Good to Great"</a> book</li> <li><a href= "https://www.amazon.com/Appreciative-Leadership-Performance-Thriving-Organization/dp/0071714065"> "Appreciative Leadership"</a> book</li> </ul>]]></description>

      <title>EP211 Decoding the Underground: Google's Dual-Lens Threat Intelligence Magic</title>
      <itunes:title>EP211 Decoding the Underground: Google&#39;s Dual-Lens Threat Intelligence Magic</itunes:title>
      <pubDate>Mon, 17 Feb 2025 15:11:00 +0000</pubDate>
      <guid isPermaLink="false"><![CDATA[ba0da4d2-b32b-4a5c-9585-f1316b263e36]]></guid>
      <link><![CDATA[https://cloudsecuritypodcast.libsyn.com/ep211-decoding-the-underground-googles-dual-lens-threat-intelligence-magic]]></link>
      <description><![CDATA[<p dir="ltr">Guest:</p> <ul> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation"><a href= "https://www.linkedin.com/in/kimberlygoody/">Kimberly Goody</a>, Head of Intel Analysis and Production, Google Cloud</li> </ul> <p dir="ltr">Topics:</p> <ul> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation">Google's Threat Intelligence Group (GTIG) has a unique position, accessing both underground forum data and incident response information. How does this dual perspective enhance your ability to identify and attribute cybercriminal campaigns?</li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation">Attributing cyberattacks with high confidence is important. Can you walk us through the process GTIG uses to connect an incident to specific threat actors, given the complexities of the threat landscape and the challenges of linking tools and actors? </li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation">There is a difficulty of correlating publicly known tool names with the aliases used by threat actors in underground forums. How does GTIG overcome this challenge to track the evolution and usage of malware and other tools? Can you give a specific example of how this "decoding" process works?</li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation">How does GTIG collaborate with other teams within Google, such as incident response or product security, to share threat intelligence and improve Google's overall security posture? How does this work make Google more secure?</li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation">What does Google (and specifically GTIG) do differently than other organizations focused on collecting and analyzing threat-intelligence? Is there AI involved?</li> </ul> <p dir="ltr">Resources:</p> <ul> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation"><a href= "https://cloud.google.com/blog/topics/threat-intelligence/cybercrime-multifaceted-national-security-threat"> "Cybercrime: A Multifaceted National Security Threat"</a> report</li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation"><a href= "https://cloud.withgoogle.com/cloudsecurity/podcast/ep112-threat-horizons-how-google-does-threat-intelligence/"> EP112 Threat Horizons - How Google Does Threat Intelligence</a></li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation"><a href= "https://cloud.withgoogle.com/cloudsecurity/podcast/ep175-meet-crystal-lister-from-public-sector-to-google-cloud-security-and-threat-horizons/"> EP175 Meet Crystal Lister: From Public Sector to Google Cloud Security and Threat Horizons</a></li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation"><a href= "https://cloud.withgoogle.com/cloudsecurity/podcast/ep178-meet-brandon-wood-the-human-side-of-threat-intelligence-from-bad-ip-to-trafficking-busts/"> EP178 Meet Brandon Wood: The Human Side of Threat Intelligence: From Bad IP to Trafficking Busts</a></li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation"><a href= "https://www.amazon.com/Wild-Swans-Three-Daughters-China/dp/0743246985"> "Wild Swans: Three Daughters of China"</a> book</li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation"><a href= "https://cloud.google.com/transform/how-google-does-it-modernizing-threat-detection"> How Google Does It: Making threat detection high-quality, scalable, and modern</a></li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation"><a href= "https://cloud.google.com/transform/how-google-does-it-vulnerability-detection-remediation/"> How Google Does It: Finding, tracking, and fixing vulnerabilities</a></li> <li><a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=NtANWZPHUak">"From Credit Cards to Crypto: The Evolution of Cybercrime"</a> video</li> </ul>]]></description>

      <title>EP209 vCISO in the Cloud: Navigating the New Security Landscape (and Don't Forget Resilience!)</title>
      <itunes:title>EP209 vCISO in the Cloud: Navigating the New Security Landscape (and Don&#39;t Forget Resilience!)</itunes:title>
      <pubDate>Mon, 03 Feb 2025 15:11:00 +0000</pubDate>
      <guid isPermaLink="false"><![CDATA[720ac65b-fcaa-49cc-973d-fe31ea42dec2]]></guid>
      <link><![CDATA[https://cloudsecuritypodcast.libsyn.com/ep209-vciso-in-the-cloud-navigating-the-new-security-landscape-and-dont-forget-resilience]]></link>
      <description><![CDATA[<p dir="ltr">Guests: </p> <ul> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation"><a href= "https://www.linkedin.com/in/beth-cartier-b520b426/">Beth Cartier</a>, former CISO, vCISO, founder of Initiative Security<strong><br /></strong></li> </ul> <p dir="ltr">Guest host of the CISO mini-series:</p> <ul> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation"><a href= "https://www.linkedin.com/in/marinakaganovich/">Marina Kaganovich</a>, Executive Trust Lead, Office of the CISO @ Google Cloud</li> </ul> <p dir="ltr">Topics:</p> <ul> <li dir="ltr">How is that vCISO'ing going? What is special about vCISO and cloud? Is it easier or harder?</li> <li dir="ltr">AI, cyber, resilience - all are hot topics these days.  In the context of cloud security, how are you seeing organizations realistically address these trends? Are they being managed effectively (finally?) or is security always playing catch up?</li> <li dir="ltr">Recent events reminded us that cybersecurity may sometimes interfere with resilience.       <guid isPermaLink="false"><![CDATA[fc9b8da7-c639-4b08-a902-a190cdfd676e]]></guid>

      <description><![CDATA[<p dir="ltr">Guest:</p> <ul> <li dir="ltr" aria-level="1"> <p dir="ltr" role="presentation"><a href= "https://www.linkedin.com/in/richmogull/">Rich Mogull</a>, SVP of Cloud Security at Firemon and CEO at <a href= "https://securosis.com/">Securosis</a></p> </li> </ul> <p dir="ltr">Topics:</p> <ul> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation">Let's talk about cloud security shared responsibility.  How to separate the blame?       <title>EP200 Zero Touch Prod, Security Rings, and Foundational Services: How Google Does Workload Security</title>
      <itunes:title>EP200 Zero Touch Prod, Security Rings, and Foundational Services: How Google Does Workload Security</itunes:title>
      <pubDate>Mon, 25 Nov 2024 15:11:00 +0000</pubDate>
      <guid isPermaLink="false"><![CDATA[0b472156-a223-4055-9838-96e056dd081b]]></guid>
      <link><![CDATA[https://cloudsecuritypodcast.libsyn.com/ep200-zero-touch-prod-security-rings-and-foundational-services-how-google-does-workload-security]]></link>
      <description><![CDATA[<p dir="ltr">Guest:</p> <ul> <li dir="ltr" aria-level="1"> <p dir="ltr" role="presentation"><a href= "https://www.linkedin.com/in/mczapinski/">Michael Czapinski</a>, Security & Reliability Enthusiast, Google</p> </li> </ul> <p dir="ltr">Topics:</p> <ul> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation"><a href= "https://cloud.google.com/docs/security/production-services-protection"> "How Google protects its production services"</a> paper covers how Google's infrastructure balances several crucial aspects, including security, reliability, development speed, and maintainability. How do you prioritize these competing demands in a real-world setting?</li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation">What attack vectors do you consider most critical in the production environment, and how has Google's defenses against these vectors improved over time?</li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation">Can you elaborate on the concept of Foundational services and their significance in Google's security posture?</li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation">How does your security approach adapt to this vast spectrum of sensitivity and purpose of our servers and services, actually?</li> <li       <title>EP197 SIEM (Decoupled or Not), and Security Data Lakes: A Google SecOps Perspective</title>
      <itunes:title>EP197 SIEM (Decoupled or Not), and Security Data Lakes: A Google SecOps Perspective</itunes:title>
      <pubDate>Mon, 04 Nov 2024 14:11:00 +0000</pubDate>
      <guid isPermaLink="false"><![CDATA[2fc85410-6a57-4777-80eb-4ada367f1121]]></guid>
      <link><![CDATA[https://cloudsecuritypodcast.libsyn.com/ep197-siem-decoupled-or-not-and-security-data-lakes-a-google-secops-perspective]]></link>
      <description><![CDATA[<p dir="ltr">Guest: </p> <ul> <li dir="ltr" aria-level="1"> <p dir="ltr" role="presentation"><a href= "https://www.linkedin.com/in/travislanham/">Travis Lanham</a>, Uber Tech Lead (UTL) for Security Operations Engineering, Google Cloud</p> </li> </ul> <p dir="ltr">Topics:</p> <ul> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation">There's been a ton of discussion in the wake of the <a href="https://youtu.be/hsmssWGdDAU">three SIEM week</a> about the future of SIEM-like products. We saw a lot of takes on how this augurs the future of <a href= "https://medium.com/anton-on-security/decoupled-siem-brilliant-or-stupid-ada2c3142b2b">disassembled or decoupled SIEMs</a>. Can you explain what these disassembled SIEMs are all about?</li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation">What are the expected upsides of detaching your SIEM interface and security capabilities from your data backend?</li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation">Tell us about the <a href= "https://medium.com/anton-on-security/chronicle-one-year-later-antons-reflections-10386491f3cd"> early days of SecOps</a> (nee Chronicle) and why we didn't go with this approach?</li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation">What are the upsides of a tightly coupled datastore + security experience for a SIEM?</li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation">Are there more risks or negatives of the decoupled/decentralized approach?  Complexity and the need to assemble "at home" are on the list, right?</li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation">One of the 50 things Google knew to be true back in the day was that product innovation comes from technical innovation, what's the technical innovation driving decoupled SIEMs?</li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation">So what about those security data lakes?       <title>EP194 Deep Dive into ADR - Application Detection and Response</title>
      <itunes:title>EP194 Deep Dive into ADR - Application Detection and Response</itunes:title>
      <pubDate>Mon, 14 Oct 2024 14:11:00 +0000</pubDate>
      <guid isPermaLink="false"><![CDATA[d10f8e5d-8c25-457d-82aa-d3f1416aa96c]]></guid>
      <link><![CDATA[https://cloudsecuritypodcast.libsyn.com/ep194-deep-dive-into-adr-application-detection-and-response]]></link>
      <description><![CDATA[<p dir="ltr">Guest:</p> <ul> <li dir="ltr" aria-level="1"> <p dir="ltr" role="presentation"><a href= "https://www.linkedin.com/in/daniel-shechter/">Daniel Shechter</a>, Co-Founder and CEO at <a href="https://www.miggo.io/">Miggo Security</a></p> </li> </ul> <p dir="ltr">Topics:</p> <ul> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation">Why do we need Application Detection and Response (ADR)? BTW, how do you define it?</li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation">Isn't ADR a subset of CDR (for cloud)?  What is the key difference that sets ADR apart from traditional EDR and CDR tools?</li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation">Why can't I just send my application data - or eBPF traces - to my SIEM and achieve the goals of ADR that way?</li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation">We had RASP and it failed due to instrumentation complexities. How does an ADR solution address these challenges and make it easier for security teams to adopt and implement?</li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation">What are the key inputs into an ADR tool?</li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation">Can you explain how your ADR correlates cloud, container, and application contexts to provide a better  view of threats? Could you share real-world examples of types of badness solved for users?</li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation">How would ADR work with other application security technologies like DAST/SAST, WAF and ASPM?</li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation">What are your thoughts on the evolution of ADR?</li> </ul> <p dir="ltr">Resources:</p> <ul> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation"><a href= "https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1dlT7Cwf4A_PCuAQQ7rMRklSdtK0IxJgULBYgbB_UFNU/edit?resourcekey=0-bF-89cS35lX2HPSzU5_S_w#gid=0"> EP157 Decoding CDR & CIRA: What Happens When SecOps Meets Cloud</a></li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation"><a href= "https://cloud.withgoogle.com/cloudsecurity/podcast/ep143-cloud-security-remediation-the-biggest-headache/"> EP143 Cloud Security Remediation: The Biggest Headache?</a></li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation"><a href= "https://www.miggo.io/resources/albeast-security-advisory-alb-vulnerability"> Miggo research re: vulnerability ALBeast</a></li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation"><a href= "https://medium.com/anton-on-security/whatdr-or-what-detection-domain-needs-its-own-tools-59cb778f5d06"> "WhatDR or What Detection Domain Needs Its Own Tools?"</a> blog</li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation"><a href= "https://betterappsec.com/making-sense-of-the-application-security-product-market-b659a8e81b6b"> "Making Sense of the Application Security Product Market"</a> blog</li> <li><a href= "https://www.amazon.com/Effective-Vulnerability-Management-Vulnerable-Ecosystem/dp/1394221207"> "Effective Vulnerability Management: Managing Risk in the Vulnerable Digital Ecosystem"</a> book</li> </ul>]]></description>

      <title>EP188 Beyond the Buzzwords: Identity's True Role in Cloud and SaaS Security</title>
      <itunes:title>EP188 Beyond the Buzzwords: Identity&#39;s True Role in Cloud and SaaS Security</itunes:title>
      <pubDate>Mon, 02 Sep 2024 14:11:00 +0000</pubDate>
      <guid isPermaLink="false"><![CDATA[58ccbe62-96a4-44d4-ba11-8eb5ba51d750]]></guid>

      <description><![CDATA[<p dir="ltr">Guest:</p> <ul> <li dir="ltr" aria-level="1"> <p dir="ltr" role="presentation"><a href= "https://www.linkedin.com/in/fledel/">Dor Fledel</a>, Founder and CEO of Spera Security, now Sr Director of Product Management at Okta</p> </li> </ul> <p dir="ltr">Topics:</p> <ul> <li dir="ltr" aria-level="1"> <p dir="ltr" role="presentation">We say "identity is the new perimeter," but I think there's a lof of  nuance to it.
