      <title>EP185 SAIF-powered Collaboration to Secure AI:  CoSAI and Why It Matters to You</title>
      <itunes:title>EP185 SAIF-powered Collaboration to Secure AI:  CoSAI and Why It Matters to You</itunes:title>
      <pubDate>Mon, 12 Aug 2024 14:11:00 +0000</pubDate>
      <guid isPermaLink="false"><![CDATA[846c5382-651f-4619-8467-dd49fe15f82f]]></guid>
      <link><![CDATA[https://cloudsecuritypodcast.libsyn.com/ep185-saif-powered-collaboration-to-secure-ai-cosai-and-why-it-matters-to-you]]></link>
      <description><![CDATA[<p dir="ltr">Guest: </p> <ul> <li dir="ltr" aria-level="1"> <p dir="ltr" role="presentation"><a href= "https://www.linkedin.com/in/labianca/">David LaBianca</a>, Senior Engineering Director, Google</p> </li> </ul> <p><strong> </strong>Topics:</p> <ul> <li dir="ltr" aria-level="1"> <p dir="ltr" role="presentation">The universe of AI risks is broad and deep. We've made a lot of headway with our SAIF framework: can you give us a) a 90 second tour of <a href= "https://safety.google/cybersecurity-advancements/saif/">SAIF</a> and b) share how it's gotten so much traction and c) talk about where we go next with it?</p> </li> <li dir="ltr" aria-level="1"> <p dir="ltr" role="presentation"><a href= "https://www.coalitionforsecureai.org/about/">The Coalition for Secure AI (CoSAI)</a> is a collaborative effort to address AI security challenges. What are Google's specific goals and expectations for CoSAI, and how will its success be measured in the long term?</p> </li> <li dir="ltr" aria-level="1"> <p dir="ltr" role="presentation">Something we love about CoSAI is that we involved some unexpected folks, notably Microsoft and OpenAI. How did that come about?</p> </li> <li dir="ltr" aria-level="1"> <p dir="ltr" role="presentation">How do we plan to work with existing organizations, such as <a href= "https://www.frontiermodelforum.org/">Frontier Model Forum (FMF)</a> and <a href="https://openssf.org/">Open Source Security Foundation (OpenSSF)</a>? Does this also complement emerging AI security standards?</p> </li> <li dir="ltr" aria-level="1"> <p dir="ltr" role="presentation">AI is moving quickly. How do we intend to keep up with the pace of change when it comes to emerging threat techniques and actors in the landscape?</p> </li> <li dir="ltr" aria-level="1"> <p dir="ltr" role="presentation">What do we expect to see out of CoSAI work and when? What should people be looking forward to and what are you most looking forward to releasing from the group?</p> </li> <li dir="ltr" aria-level="1"> <p dir="ltr" role="presentation">We have proposed projects for CoSAI, including developing a defender's framework and addressing software supply chain security for AI systems. How can others use them?  In other words, if I am a mid-sized bank CISO, do I care? How do I benefit from it?</p> </li> <li dir="ltr" aria-level="1"> <p dir="ltr" role="presentation">An off-the-cuff question, how to do AI governance well?<strong> </strong></p> </li> </ul> <p dir="ltr">Resources:</p> <ul> <li dir="ltr" aria-level="1"> <p dir="ltr" role="presentation"><a href= "https://www.coalitionforsecureai.org/">CoSAI</a> site, <a href= "https://blog.google/technology/safety-security/google-coalition-for-secure-ai/"> CoSAI 3 projects</a></p> </li> <li dir="ltr" aria-level="1"> <p dir="ltr" role="presentation"><a href= "https://safety.google/cybersecurity-advancements/saif/">SAIF main site</a></p> </li> <li dir="ltr" aria-level="1"> <p dir="ltr" role="presentation"><a href= "https://cloud.google.com/transform/gen-ai-governance-10-tips-to-level-up-your-ai-program"> Gen AI governance: 10 tips to level up your AI program</a></p> </li> <li dir="ltr" aria-level="1"> <p dir="ltr" role="presentation"><a href= "https://cloud.google.com/blog/transform/prompt-what-think-about-when-youre-thinking-about-securing-ai"> "Securing AI: Similar or Different?"</a> paper</p> </li> <li dir="ltr" aria-level="1"> <p dir="ltr" role="presentation"><a href= "https://medium.com/anton-on-security/our-security-of-ai-papers-and-blogs-explained-7e50afc0469b"> Our Security of AI Papers and Blogs Explained</a></p> </li> </ul> <p> </p>]]></description>
      
      <content:encoded><![CDATA[<p dir="ltr">Guest: </p> <ul> <li dir="ltr" aria-level="1"> <p dir="ltr" role="presentation"><a href= "https://www.linkedin.com/in/labianca/">David LaBianca</a>, Senior Engineering Director, Google</p> </li> </ul> <p> Topics:</p> <ul> <li dir="ltr" aria-level="1"> <p dir="ltr" role="presentation">The universe of AI risks is broad and deep.       <title>EP182 ITDR: The Missing Piece in Your Security Puzzle or Yet Another Tool to Buy?</title>
      <itunes:title>EP182 ITDR: The Missing Piece in Your Security Puzzle or Yet Another Tool to Buy?</itunes:title>
      <pubDate>Mon, 22 Jul 2024 14:11:00 +0000</pubDate>
      <guid isPermaLink="false"><![CDATA[4d971cae-5a24-49a1-a1b2-c01b8591f19c]]></guid>
      <link><![CDATA[https://cloudsecuritypodcast.libsyn.com/ep182-itdr-the-missing-piece-in-your-security-puzzle-or-yet-another-tool-to-buy]]></link>
      <description><![CDATA[<p dir="ltr">Guest:</p> <ul> <li dir="ltr" aria-level="1"> <p dir="ltr" role="presentation"><a href= "https://www.linkedin.com/in/a-bateman/">Adam Bateman</a>, Co-founder and CEO, Push Security</p> </li> </ul> <p dir="ltr">Topics:</p> <ul> <li dir="ltr" aria-level="1"> <p dir="ltr" role="presentation">What is Identity Threat Detection and Response (<a href= "https://www.gartner.com/en/newsroom/press-releases/2022-03-07-gartner-identifies-top-security-and-risk-management-trends-for-2022">ITDR</a>)? How do you define it?</p> </li> <li dir="ltr" aria-level="1"> <p dir="ltr" role="presentation">What gets better at a client organization once ITDR is deployed?</p> </li> <li dir="ltr" aria-level="1"> <p dir="ltr" role="presentation">Do we also need  "ISPM" (parallel to CDR/CSPM), and what about CIEM?</p> </li> <li dir="ltr" aria-level="1"> <p dir="ltr" role="presentation">Workload identity ITDR vs human identity ITDR? Do we need both? Are these the same?</p> </li> <li dir="ltr" aria-level="1"> <p dir="ltr" role="presentation">What are the alternatives to using ITDR? Can't SIEM/UEBA help - perhaps with browser logs?</p> </li> <li dir="ltr" aria-level="1"> <p dir="ltr" role="presentation">What are some of the common types of identity-based threats that ITDR can help detect?</p> </li> <li dir="ltr" aria-level="1"> <p dir="ltr" role="presentation">What advice would you give to organizations that are considering implementing ITDR?</p> </li> </ul> <p dir="ltr">Resources:</p> <ul> <li dir="ltr" aria-level="1"> <p dir="ltr" role="presentation"><a href= "https://www.gartner.com/en/newsroom/press-releases/04-12-2023-gartner-identifies-the-top-cybersecurity-trends-for-2023"> ITDR Definition</a></p> </li> <li dir="ltr" aria-level="1"> <p dir="ltr" role="presentation"><a href= "https://pushsecurity.com/blog/what-is-itdr-identity-threat-detection-response/"> ITDR blog by Push / solve problem</a></p> </li> </ul> <p> </p>]]></description>
      
      <content:encoded><![CDATA[<p dir="ltr">Guest:</p> <ul> <li dir="ltr" aria-level="1"> <p dir="ltr" role="presentation"><a href= "https://www.linkedin.com/in/a-bateman/">Adam Bateman</a>, Co-founder and CEO, Push Security</p> </li> </ul> <p dir="ltr">Topics:</p> <ul> <li dir="ltr" aria-level="1"> <p dir="ltr" role="presentation">What is Identity Threat Detection and Response (<a href= "https://www.gartner.com/en/newsroom/press-releases/2022-03-07-gartner-identifies-top-security-and-risk-management-trends-for-2022">ITDR</a>)?       <itunes:title>EP173 SAIF in Focus: 5 AI Security Risks and SAIF Mitigations</itunes:title>
      <pubDate>Mon, 20 May 2024 14:11:00 +0000</pubDate>
      <guid isPermaLink="false"><![CDATA[7bb90689-bee9-4106-bc86-fc98678c9088]]></guid>
      <link><![CDATA[https://cloudsecuritypodcast.libsyn.com/ep173-saif-in-focus-5-ai-security-risks-and-saif-mitigations]]></link>
      <description><![CDATA[<p dir="ltr">Guest:</p> <ul> <li dir="ltr" aria-level="1"> <p dir="ltr" role="presentation"><a href= "https://www.linkedin.com/in/shanrao/">Shan  Rao</a>, Group Product Manager, Google<strong> </strong></p> </li> </ul> <p dir="ltr">Topics:</p> <ul> <li dir="ltr" aria-level="1"> <p dir="ltr" role="presentation">What are the unique challenges when securing AI for cloud environments, compared to traditional IT systems?</p> </li> <li dir="ltr" aria-level="1"> <p dir="ltr" role="presentation"><a href= "https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2xSNyfAbWb8">Your talk</a> covers 5 risks, why did you pick these five? What are the five, and are these the worst?</p> </li> <li dir="ltr" aria-level="1"> <p dir="ltr" role="presentation">Some of the mitigation seems the same for all risks. What are the popular <a href= "https://safety.google/cybersecurity-advancements/saif/">SAIF</a> mitigations that cover more of the risks?</p> </li> <li dir="ltr" aria-level="1"> <p dir="ltr" role="presentation">Can we move quickly and securely with AI?       <title>EP155 Cyber, Geopolitics, AI, Cloud - All in One Book?</title>

      <pubDate>Mon, 15 Jan 2024 15:11:00 +0000</pubDate>
      <guid isPermaLink="false"><![CDATA[77ee728d-278e-42e2-b9ac-050fa5c27cbc]]></guid>

      <description><![CDATA[<p dir="ltr">Guests:</p> <ul> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation"><a href= "https://usnwc.edu/Faculty-and-Departments/Directory/Derek-S-Reveron"> Derek Reveron</a>, Professor and Chair of National Security at the US Naval War College</li> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation"><a href= "https://professional.brown.edu/people/john-savage">John Savage</a>, An Wang Professor Emeritus of Computer Science of Brown University</li> </ul> <p dir="ltr">Topics:</p> <ul> <li dir="ltr" aria-level="1"> <p dir="ltr" role="presentation">You wrote <a href= "https://www.amazon.com/Security-Cyber-Age-Derek-Reveron/dp/1009308580/"> a book on cyber and war</a>, how did this come about and what did you most enjoy learning from the other during the writing process?</p> </li> <li dir="ltr" aria-level="1"> <p dir="ltr" role="presentation">Is generative AI going to be a game changer in international relations and war, or is it just another tool?</p> </li> <li dir="ltr" aria-level="1"> <p dir="ltr" role="presentation">You also touch briefly on lethal autonomous weapons systems and ethics–that feels like the genie is right in the very neck of the bottle right now, is it too late?</p> </li> <li dir="ltr" aria-level="1"> <p dir="ltr" role="presentation">Aside from this book, and the awesome course you offered at Brown that sparked Tim's interest in this field, how can we democratize this space better? </p> </li> <li dir="ltr" aria-level="1"> <p dir="ltr" role="presentation">How does the emergence and shift to Cloud impact security in the cyber age?</p> </li> <li dir="ltr" aria-level="1"> <p dir="ltr" role="presentation">What are your thoughts on the intersection of Cloud as a set of technologies and operating model and state security (like sovereignty)?       <title>EP149 Canned Detections: From Educational Samples to Production-Ready Code</title>
      <itunes:title>EP149 Canned Detections: From Educational Samples to Production-Ready Code</itunes:title>
      <pubDate>Mon, 20 Nov 2023 15:11:00 +0000</pubDate>
      <guid isPermaLink="false"><![CDATA[d5c73f2a-847e-47bf-8614-08bdabd655d0]]></guid>
      <link><![CDATA[https://cloudsecuritypodcast.libsyn.com/ep149-canned-detections-from-educational-samples-to-production-ready-code]]></link>

      <title>EP147 Special: 2024 Google Cloud Security Forecast Report</title>
      <itunes:title>EP147 Special: 2024 Google Cloud Security Forecast Report</itunes:title>
      <pubDate>Wed, 08 Nov 2023 16:35:00 +0000</pubDate>
      <guid isPermaLink="false"><![CDATA[9a65703e-f3cb-4255-8a3e-bb44d5804bed]]></guid>

      <description><![CDATA[<p dir="ltr">Guest: </p> <ul> <li dir="ltr" aria-level="1"> <p dir="ltr" role="presentation"><a href= "https://moma.corp.google.com/person/kelliv">Kelli Vanderlee</a>, Senior Manager, Threat Analysis, Mandiant at Google Cloud</p> </li> </ul> <p dir="ltr">Topics:</p> <ul> <li dir="ltr" aria-level="1"> <p dir="ltr" role="presentation">Can you really forecast threats? Or as Tim would say it, what gets better once you read it?</p> </li> <li dir="ltr" aria-level="1"> <p dir="ltr" role="presentation">What is the threat forecast for cloud environments? It says <em>"Cyber attacks targeting hybrid and multi-cloud environments will mature and become more impactful"</em> - what does it mean?</p> </li> <li dir="ltr" aria-level="1"> <p dir="ltr" role="presentation">Of course AI makes an appearance as well: <em>"LLMs and other gen AI tools will likely be developed and offered as a service to assist attackers with target compromises."</em> Do we really expect attacker-run LLM SaaS? Will it be good?</p> </li> <li dir="ltr" aria-level="1"> <p dir="ltr" role="presentation">There are a number of significant elections scheduled for 2024, are there implications for cloud security?</p> </li> <li dir="ltr" aria-level="1"> <p dir="ltr" role="presentation">Based on the threat information, tell me about something that is going well, what will get better in 2024?</p> </li> </ul> <p dir="ltr">Resources:</p> <ul> <li dir="ltr" aria-level="1"> <p dir="ltr" role="presentation"><a href= "https://cloud.google.com/resources/security/cybersecurity-forecast"> 2024 Google Cloud Security Forecast Report</a></p> </li> <li dir="ltr" aria-level="1"> <p dir="ltr" role="presentation"><a href= "https://cloud.withgoogle.com/cloudsecurity/podcast/ep112-threat-horizons-how-google-does-threat-intelligence/"> EP112 Threat Horizons - How Google Does Threat Intelligence</a></p> </li> <li dir="ltr" aria-level="1"> <p dir="ltr" role="presentation"><a href= "https://cloud.withgoogle.com/cloudsecurity/podcast/ep135-ai-and-security-the-good-the-bad-and-the-magical/"> EP135 AI and Security: The Good, the Bad, and the Magical</a></p> </li> <li dir="ltr" aria-level="1"> <p dir="ltr" role="presentation"><a href= "https://www.mandiant.com/resources/Infographics/how-stop-ransomware-attack"> How to Stop a Ransomware Attack</a></p> </li> <li dir="ltr" aria-level="1"> <p dir="ltr" role="presentation"><a href= "https://www.zetter-zeroday.com/p/sophisticated-stripedfly-spy-platform"> Sophisticated StripedFly Spy Platform Masqueraded for Years as Crypto Miner</a></p> </li> </ul> <p> </p>]]></description>
      
      <content:encoded><![CDATA[<p dir="ltr">Guest: </p> <ul> <li dir="ltr" aria-level="1"> <p dir="ltr" role="presentation"><a href= "https://moma.corp.google.com/person/kelliv">Kelli Vanderlee</a>, Senior Manager, Threat Analysis, Mandiant at Google Cloud</p> </li> </ul> <p dir="ltr">Topics:</p> <ul> <li dir="ltr" aria-level="1"> <p dir="ltr" role="presentation">Can you really forecast threats? Or as Tim would say it, what gets better once you read it?</p> </li> <li dir="ltr" aria-level="1"> <p dir="ltr" role="presentation">What is the threat forecast for cloud environments? It says <em>"Cyber attacks targeting hybrid and multi-cloud environments will mature and become more impactful"</em> - what does it mean?</p> </li> <li dir="ltr" aria-level="1"> <p dir="ltr" role="presentation">Of course AI makes an appearance as well: <em>"LLMs and other gen AI tools will likely be developed and offered as a service to assist attackers with target compromises."</em> Do we really expect attacker-run LLM SaaS? What models will they use? Will it be good?</p> </li> <li dir="ltr" aria-level="1"> <p dir="ltr" role="presentation">There are a number of significant elections scheduled for 2024, are there implications for cloud security?</p> </li> <li dir="ltr" aria-level="1"> <p dir="ltr" role="presentation">Based on the threat information, tell me about something that is going well, what will get better in 2024?</p> </li> </ul> <p dir="ltr">Resources:</p> <ul> <li dir="ltr" aria-level="1"> <p dir="ltr" role="presentation"><a href= "https://cloud.google.com/resources/security/cybersecurity-forecast"> 2024 Google Cloud Security Forecast Report</a></p> </li> <li dir="ltr" aria-level="1"> <p dir="ltr" role="presentation"><a href= "https://cloud.withgoogle.com/cloudsecurity/podcast/ep112-threat-horizons-how-google-does-threat-intelligence/"> EP112 Threat Horizons - How Google Does Threat Intelligence</a></p> </li> <li dir="ltr" aria-level="1"> <p dir="ltr" role="presentation"><a href= "https://cloud.withgoogle.com/cloudsecurity/podcast/ep135-ai-and-security-the-good-the-bad-and-the-magical/"> EP135 AI and Security: The Good, the Bad, and the Magical</a></p> </li> <li dir="ltr" aria-level="1"> <p dir="ltr" role="presentation"><a href= "https://www.mandiant.com/resources/Infographics/how-stop-ransomware-attack"> How to Stop a Ransomware Attack</a></p> </li> <li dir="ltr" aria-level="1"> <p dir="ltr" role="presentation"><a href= "https://www.zetter-zeroday.com/p/sophisticated-stripedfly-spy-platform"> Sophisticated StripedFly Spy Platform Masqueraded for Years as Crypto Miner</a></p> </li> </ul> <p> </p>]]></content:encoded>

      <title>EP144  LLMs: A Double-Edged Sword for Cloud Security? Weighing the Benefits and Risks of Large Language Models</title>
      <itunes:title>EP144  LLMs: A Double-Edged Sword for Cloud Security? Weighing the Benefits and Risks of Large Language Models</itunes:title>
      <pubDate>Mon, 23 Oct 2023 14:11:00 +0000</pubDate>
      <guid isPermaLink="false"><![CDATA[d0c8efb3-3ed7-4312-9435-6bf357e7fdfd]]></guid>
      <link><![CDATA[https://cloudsecuritypodcast.libsyn.com/ep144-llms-a-double-edged-sword-for-cloud-security-weighing-the-benefits-and-risks-of-large-language-models]]></link>
      <description><![CDATA[<p dir="ltr">Guest:</p> <ul> <li dir="ltr" aria-level="1"> <p dir="ltr" role="presentation"><a href= "https://www.linkedin.com/in/kathryn-shih-57803617/">Kathryn Shih</a>, Group Product Manager, LLM Lead in Google Cloud Security</p> </li> </ul> <p dir="ltr">Topics:</p> <ul> <li dir="ltr" aria-level="1"> <p dir="ltr" role="presentation">Could you give our audience the quick version of what is an LLM and what things can they do vs not do?  Is this "baby AGI" or is this a glorified "autocomplete"?</p> </li> <li dir="ltr" aria-level="1"> <p dir="ltr" role="presentation">Let's talk about the different ways to tune the models, and when we think about tuning what are the ways that attackers might influence or steal our data?</p> </li> <li dir="ltr" aria-level="1"> <p dir="ltr" role="presentation">Can you help our security listener leaders have the right vocabulary and concepts to reason about the risk of their information a) going into an LLM and b) getting regurgitated by one?</p> </li> <li dir="ltr" aria-level="1"> <p dir="ltr" role="presentation">How do I keep the output of a model safe, and what questions do I need to ask a vendor to understand if they're a) talking nonsense or b) actually keeping their output safe? </p> </li> <li dir="ltr" aria-level="1"> <p dir="ltr" role="presentation">Are hallucinations inherent to LLMs and can they ever be fixed?</p> </li> <li dir="ltr" aria-level="1"> <p dir="ltr" role="presentation">So there are risks to data and new opportunities for attacks and hallucinations. How do we know good opportunities in the area given the risks? </p> </li> </ul> <p dir="ltr">Resources:</p> <ul> <li dir="ltr" aria-level="1"> <p dir="ltr" role="presentation"><a href= "https://arxiv.org/abs/2005.11401v4">Retrieval Augmented Generation</a> (or go ask <a href= "https://bard.google.com/">Bard</a> about it)<strong id= "docs-internal-guid-ec777aba-7fff-122a-c68b-0a5e6c3c6470"></strong></p> </li> <li dir="ltr" aria-level="1"> <p dir="ltr" role="presentation"><strong id= "docs-internal-guid-ec777aba-7fff-122a-c68b-0a5e6c3c6470"></strong><a href="https://medium.com/anton-on-security/new-paper-securing-ai-similar-or-different-91f3bdac1eff">"New Paper: "Securing AI: Similar or Different?""</a>  blog</p> </li> </ul>]]></description>
      
      <content:encoded><![CDATA[<p dir="ltr">Guest:</p> <ul> <li dir="ltr" aria-level="1"> <p dir="ltr" role="presentation"><a href= "https://www.linkedin.com/in/kathryn-shih-57803617/">Kathryn Shih</a>, Group Product Manager, LLM Lead in Google Cloud Security</p> </li> </ul> <p dir="ltr">Topics:</p> <ul> <li dir="ltr" aria-level="1"> <p dir="ltr" role="presentation">Could you give our audience the quick version of what is an LLM and what things can they do vs not do?       <title>EP134  How to Prioritize UX and Security in the Cloud: UX as a Security Capability</title>
      <itunes:title>EP134  How to Prioritize UX and Security in the Cloud: UX as a Security Capability</itunes:title>
      <pubDate>Mon, 14 Aug 2023 14:11:00 +0000</pubDate>
      <guid isPermaLink="false"><![CDATA[4d973076-1065-4a5c-8067-04003ce35179]]></guid>
      <link><![CDATA[https://cloudsecuritypodcast.libsyn.com/ep134-how-to-prioritize-ux-and-security-in-the-cloud-ux-as-a-security-capability]]></link>
      <description><![CDATA[<p dir="ltr">Guest: </p> <ul> <li dir="ltr" aria-level="1"> <p dir="ltr" role="presentation"><a href= "https://www.linkedin.com/in/stephaniehay/">Steph Hay</a> , Director of UX, Google Cloud Security</p> </li> </ul> <p dir="ltr">Topics:</p> <ul> <li dir="ltr" aria-level="1"> <p dir="ltr" role="presentation">The importance of User Experience (UX) in security is so obvious – though it isn't to a lot of people! Could we talk about the importance of UX in security?</p> </li> <li dir="ltr" aria-level="1"> <p dir="ltr" role="presentation">UX and security in general have an uneasy relationship, and security is harmed by bad UX, it also feels like bad UX can be a security issue. What is your take on this?</p> </li> <li dir="ltr" aria-level="1"> <p dir="ltr" role="presentation">How do you think about prioritizing your team's time between day zero vs day n experiences for users of security tools?</p> </li> <li dir="ltr" aria-level="1"> <p dir="ltr" role="presentation">Some say that cloud security should be invisible, but does this mean no UX at all?       <title>EP128  Building Enterprise Threat Intelligence: The Who, What, Where, and Why</title>
      <itunes:title>EP128  Building Enterprise Threat Intelligence: The Who, What, Where, and Why</itunes:title>
      <pubDate>Mon, 03 Jul 2023 14:11:00 +0000</pubDate>
      <guid isPermaLink="false"><![CDATA[25cc30af-5d59-442c-b825-91f7d5a1c484]]></guid>
      <link><![CDATA[https://cloudsecuritypodcast.libsyn.com/ep128-building-enterprise-threat-intelligence-the-who-what-where-and-why]]></link>
      <description><![CDATA[<p dir="ltr">Guest: </p> <ul> <li dir="ltr" aria-level="1"> <p dir="ltr" role="presentation"><a href= "https://www.linkedin.com/in/john-doyle-a02bab10/">John Doyle</a>, Principle Intelligence Enablement Consultant at Mandiant / Google Cloud</p> </li> </ul> <p><strong> </strong>Topics:</p> <ul> <li dir="ltr" aria-level="1"> <p dir="ltr" role="presentation">You have created <a href= "http://www.mandiant.com/insidethemind">a new intelligence class focused on building enterprise threat intelligence capability</a>, so what is the profile of an organization and profile for a person that benefits the most from the class?</p> </li> <li dir="ltr" aria-level="1"> <p dir="ltr" role="presentation">There are many places to learn threat intel (TI), what is special about your new class? </p> </li> <li dir="ltr" aria-level="1"> <p dir="ltr" role="presentation">You talk about country cyber operations in the class, so what is the defender - relevant difference between, say, DPRK and Iran cyber doctrines? More generally, how do defenders benefit from such per country intel?</p> </li> <li dir="ltr" aria-level="1"> <p dir="ltr" role="presentation">Can you really predict what the state-affiliated attackers would do to your organization based on the country doctrine?</p> </li> <li dir="ltr" aria-level="1"> <p dir="ltr" role="presentation">In many minds, TI is connected to attribution.       <title>EP118 RSA 2023 - How to Protect Your Organization from Cyberattacks in a Time of Political Turmoil</title>
      <itunes:title>EP118 RSA 2023 - How to Protect Your Organization from Cyberattacks in a Time of Political Turmoil</itunes:title>
      <pubDate>Mon, 24 Apr 2023 12:11:00 +0000</pubDate>
      <guid isPermaLink="false"><![CDATA[a1057aa1-199b-40b3-8ab3-d05f1e9a72b1]]></guid>
      <link><![CDATA[https://cloudsecuritypodcast.libsyn.com/ep118-rsa-2023-how-to-protect-your-organization-from-cyberattacks-in-a-time-of-political-turmoil]]></link>
      <description><![CDATA[<p dir="ltr">Guests:  </p> <ul> <li dir="ltr" aria-level="1"> <p dir="ltr" role="presentation"><a href= "https://www.linkedin.com/in/shanyn-ronis/">Shanyn Ronis</a>, Head of the Mandiant Communication Center</p> </li> <li dir="ltr" aria-level="1"> <p dir="ltr" role="presentation"><a href= "https://www.linkedin.com/in/john-m-miller/">John Miller</a>,   Head of Mandiant Intelligence Analysis</p> </li> </ul> <p dir="ltr">Topics:</p> <ul> <li dir="ltr" aria-level="1"> <p dir="ltr" role="presentation">It seems like we're seeing more cyber activity taking place in the context of geopolitical events. A lot of organizations struggle to figure out if/how to respond to these events and any related cyber activity.  What advice do you have for these organizations and their leadership?</p> </li> <li dir="ltr" aria-level="1"> <p dir="ltr" role="presentation">A  lot of threat intel (TI) suffers from "What does this event mean for threats to our organization?" - sort of how to connect CNN to your IDS? What is your best advice on this to a CISO? </p> </li> <li dir="ltr" aria-level="1"> <p dir="ltr" role="presentation">TI also suffers from "1. Get TI 2. ??? 3. Profit!" - how does your model help organizations avoid this trap? </p> </li> <li dir="ltr" aria-level="1"> <p dir="ltr" role="presentation">Surely there are different levels of granularity here to TI and its relevance. Is what a CISO needs different from what an IR member needs? Do you differentiate your feed along those axes?</p> </li> <li dir="ltr" aria-level="1"> <p dir="ltr" role="presentation">What does success look like?       <description><![CDATA[<p dir="ltr">Guest:</p> <ul> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation"><a href= "https://www.linkedin.com/in/hepwori/">Isaac Hepworth</a>, PM focused on Software Supply Chain Security @ Google</li> </ul> <p dir="ltr">Cooked questions:</p> <ul> <li dir="ltr" role="presentation">Why is everyone talking about SBOMs all of a sudden?       <title>EP109 How Google Does Vulnerability Management: The Not So Secret Secrets!</title>
      <itunes:title>EP109 How Google Does Vulnerability Management: The Not So Secret Secrets!</itunes:title>
      <pubDate>Mon, 20 Feb 2023 15:11:00 +0000</pubDate>
      <guid isPermaLink="false"><![CDATA[0a744812-2a05-4d19-9db7-17fb850eea48]]></guid>
      <link><![CDATA[https://cloudsecuritypodcast.libsyn.com/ep109-how-google-does-vulnerability-management-the-not-so-secret-secrets]]></link>
      <description><![CDATA[<p dir="ltr">Guest: </p> <ul> <li dir="ltr" aria-level="1"> <p dir="ltr" role="presentation"><a href= "https://www.linkedin.com/in/anaoprea/">Ana Oprea</a>, Staff Security Engineer, European Lead of Vulnerability Coordination Center @ Google</p> </li> </ul> <p dir="ltr">Topics:</p> <ul> <li dir="ltr" aria-level="1"> <p dir="ltr" role="presentation">What is the scope for the vulnerability management program at Google? Does it cover  OS, off-the-shelf applications, custom code we wrote … or all of the above?</p> </li> <li dir="ltr" aria-level="1"> <p dir="ltr" role="presentation">Our vulnerability prioritization includes a process called "impact assessment." What does our impact assessment for a vulnerability look like?</p> </li> <li dir="ltr" aria-level="1"> <p dir="ltr" role="presentation">How do we prioritize what to remediate? How do we decide on the speed of remediation needed?</p> </li> <li dir="ltr" aria-level="1"> <p dir="ltr" role="presentation">How do we know if we've done a good job?       <title>EP102 Sunil Potti on Building Cloud Security at Google</title>
      <itunes:title>EP102 Sunil Potti on Building Cloud Security at Google</itunes:title>
      <pubDate>Mon, 19 Dec 2022 15:48:00 +0000</pubDate>
      <guid isPermaLink="false"><![CDATA[3231eac0-28a0-4cbe-bb10-4b4a0d6a32e7]]></guid>
      <link><![CDATA[https://cloudsecuritypodcast.libsyn.com/ep102-sunil-potti-on-building-cloud-security-at-google]]></link>
      <description><![CDATA[<p><span style="font-weight: 400;">Guest: </span></p> <ul> <li style="font-weight: 400;" aria-level="1"><a href= "https://www.linkedin.com/in/sunilpotti"><span style= "font-weight: 400;">Sunil Potti</span></a><span style= "font-weight: 400;">, VP / GM, Google Cloud</span></li> </ul> <p><span style="font-weight: 400;">Topics:</span></p> <ul> <li style="font-weight: 400;" aria-level="1"><span style= "font-weight: 400;">One of the biggest shifts we've noticed is the shift from building security because we think security is good, to building security as a business. How did you make that cultural shift happen in our organization? </span></li> <li style="font-weight: 400;" aria-level="1"><span style= "font-weight: 400;">With organizations migrating to cloud we have a set of tradeoffs between meeting security teams where they are with on-prem expectations of security vs cloud-native approaches. How do you think about investing in next generation products vs holding the hands of CISOs just stepping into the cloud?</span></li> <li style="font-weight: 400;" aria-level="1"><span style= "font-weight: 400;">What matters more to you as a leader, secure cloud (GCP, Workspace) or security products (Chronicle SecOps, BCE, SCC, etc)?</span></li> <li style="font-weight: 400;" aria-level="1"><span style= "font-weight: 400;">Is invisible security the same as "building security in"? Aren't there security controls where the value is derived from them being visible to users?</span></li> <li style="font-weight: 400;" aria-level="1"><a href= "https://www.mandiant.com/"><span style= "font-weight: 400;">Mandiant</span></a> <span style= "font-weight: 400;">brings services expertise to Google Cloud, typically not our strong area and not our DNA, how do we plan to make the most of Mandiant within Google's culture?</span></li> </ul> <p><span style="font-weight: 400;">Resources:</span></p> <ul> <li><a href= "https://simonsinek.com/books/start-with-why/"><span style= "font-weight: 400;">Simon Sinek "Start With Why"</span></a> <span style="font-weight: 400;">book</span></li> </ul>]]></description>

How do you think about investing in next generation products vs holding the hands of CISOs just stepping into the cloud?</li> <li style="font-weight: 400;" aria-level="1">What matters more to you as a leader, secure cloud (GCP, Workspace) or security products (Chronicle SecOps, BCE, SCC, etc)?</li> <li style="font-weight: 400;" aria-level="1">Is invisible security the same as "building security in"?       <title>EP66 Is This Binary Legit? How Google Uses Binary Authorization and Code Provenance</title>
      <itunes:title>EP66 Is This Binary Legit? How Google Uses Binary Authorization and Code Provenance</itunes:title>
      <pubDate>Mon, 23 May 2022 14:26:29 +0000</pubDate>
      <guid isPermaLink="false"><![CDATA[d8c9d20d-6c05-4f10-8d48-57fecd9b2bf3]]></guid>
      <link><![CDATA[https://cloudsecuritypodcast.libsyn.com/ep66-is-this-binary-legit-how-google-uses-binary-authorization-and-code-provenance]]></link>
      <description><![CDATA[<p><span style="font-weight: 400;">Guest:</span></p> <ul> <li><span style="font-weight: 400;"><a href= "https://www.linkedin.com/in/jianingguo/">Sandra Guo</a>, Product Manager in Security, Google Cloud</span></li> </ul> <p><span style="font-weight: 400;">Topics:</span></p> <ul> <li><span style="font-weight: 400;">We have a really interesting problem here: if we make great investments in our use of trusted repositories, and great investments in doing code review on every change, and securing our build systems, and having reproducible builds, how do we know that all of what we did upstream is actually what gets deployed to production?</span></li> <li><span style="font-weight: 400;">What are the realistic threats that</span> <a href= "https://cloud.google.com/binary-authorization"><span style= "font-weight: 400;">Binary Authorization</span></a> <span style= "font-weight: 400;">handles? Are there specific organizations that are more at risk from those?</span></li> <li><span style="font-weight: 400;">What's the Google inspiration for this work, both development and adoption? </span></li> <li><span style="font-weight: 400;">How do we make this work in practice at a real organization that is not Google? </span></li> <li><span style="font-weight: 400;">Where do you see organizations "getting it wrong" and where do you see organizations "getting it right"?</span></li> <li><span style="font-weight: 400;">We've had a lot of conversations about rolling out zero-trust for enterprise applications, how do those lessons (start small, be visible, plan plan plan) translate into deploying Binauthz into blocking mode? </span></li> </ul> <p><span style="font-weight: 400;">Resources:</span></p> <ul> <li><a href= "https://cloud.google.com/docs/security/binary-authorization-for-borg"> <span style="font-weight: 400;">"Binary Authorization for Borg: how Google verifies code provenance and implements code identity"</span></a> <span style= "font-weight: 400;">paper</span></li> <li><a href= "https://cloud.google.com/binary-authorization/docs"><span style= "font-weight: 400;">Binary Authorization for deploying trusted images</span></a></li> <li><a href= "https://cloud.google.com/blog/products/devops-sre"><span style= "font-weight: 400;">DevOps & SRE</span></a> <span style= "font-weight: 400;">at Google</span></li> </ul>]]></description>
      
      <content:encoded><![CDATA[<p>Guest:</p> <ul> <li><a href= "https://www.linkedin.com/in/jianingguo/">Sandra Guo</a>, Product Manager in Security, Google Cloud</li> </ul> <p>Topics:</p> <ul> <li>We have a really interesting problem here: if we make great investments in our use of trusted repositories, and great investments in doing code review on every change, and securing our build systems, and having reproducible builds, how do we know that all of what we did upstream is actually what gets deployed to production?</li> <li>What are the realistic threats that <a href= "https://cloud.google.com/binary-authorization">Binary Authorization</a> handles? Are there specific organizations that are more at risk from those?</li> <li>What's the Google inspiration for this work, both development and adoption? </li> <li>How do we make this work in practice at a real organization that is not Google? </li> <li>Where do you see organizations "getting it wrong" and where do you see organizations "getting it right"?</li> <li>We've had a lot of conversations about rolling out zero-trust for enterprise applications, how do those lessons (start small, be visible, plan plan plan) translate into deploying Binauthz into blocking mode? </li> </ul> <p>Resources:</p> <ul> <li><a href= "https://cloud.google.com/docs/security/binary-authorization-for-borg"> "Binary Authorization for Borg: how Google verifies code provenance and implements code identity"</a> paper</li> <li><a href= "https://cloud.google.com/binary-authorization/docs">Binary Authorization for deploying trusted images</a></li> <li><a href= "https://cloud.google.com/blog/products/devops-sre">DevOps & SRE</a> at Google</li> </ul>]]></content:encoded>
